kutvā lohamayaṃ jālaṃ tasyādho jvalanaṃ dadau .. 5.25 ..
5.d:
किमेतदुच्यते भद्र प्रत्यक्षं हेतुमद्वचः ।
ततः श्रुत्वा मुनेर्विप्रं लुब्धकः प्राह धर्मवित् ।
कुत्वा लोहमयं जालं तस्याधो ज्वलनं ददौ ॥ 5.25 ॥
5.m: "What is this that is said, good sir, contrary to visible perception, though accompanied by reasoning?" / Then, hearing the brāhmaṇa sage, the hunter, knower of dharma, said: / He made an iron mesh and placed fire beneath it.

5.s:
dattvā vahniṃ dvijaṃ prāha jvālyatāṃ kāṣṭhasacayaḥ .
tato vipro mukhenāgniṃ prajvālya virarāma ha .. 5.26 ..
5.d:
दत्त्वा वह्निं द्विजं प्राह ज्वाल्यतां काष्ठसचयः ।
ततो विप्रो मुखेनाग्निं प्रज्वाल्य विरराम ह ॥ 5.26 ॥
5.m: Having applied the fire, he said to the twice-born: "Let the heap of wood be ignited." / Then the brāhmaṇa, having kindled the fire with his mouth, paused.

5.s:
jvalite tu punarvahnau taṃ jālaṃ lohasaṃbhavam .
pṛthakpṛthak sahastrāṇi ninye'ntarjālakairdvija .
ekasthānagatasyāpi vahnerāyasajālakaiḥ .. 5.27 ..
5.d:
ज्वलिते तु पुनर्वह्नौ तं जालं लोहसंभवम् ।
पृथक्पृथक् सहस्त्राणि निन्येऽन्तर्जालकैर्द्विज ।
एकस्थानगतस्यापि वह्नेरायसजालकैः ॥ 5.27 ॥
5.m: When the fire was blazing, O twice-born, through the interstices of the mesh / the hunter led that iron mesh into thousands of separate [points of heat], / even though the fire located in a single place acted through the iron meshes.

5.s:
tato lubdho'bravīdvipramekāṃ jvālāṃ mahāmune .
gṛhāṇa yena śeṣāṇāṃ kariṣyāmīha nāśanam .. 5.28 ..
5.d:
ततो लुब्धोऽब्रवीद्विप्रमेकां ज्वालां महामुने ।
गृहाण येन शेषाणां करिष्यामीह नाशनम् ॥ 5.28 ॥
5.m: Then the hunter said to the brāhmaṇa: "O great sage, catch hold of / one flame, so that I may destroy the rest here."

5.s:
evamuktvā hutāśe tu toyapūrṇaṃ ghaṭaṃ drutam .
cikṣepa sahasā vahniḥ praśaśāmāśu pūrvavat .. 5.29 ..
5.d:
एवमुक्त्वा हुताशे तु तोयपूर्णं घटं द्रुतम् ।
चिक्षेप सहसा वह्निः प्रशशामाशु पूर्ववत् ॥ 5.29 ॥
5.m: Having spoken thus, he quickly threw a jar filled with water / onto the fire; suddenly the fire was quickly extinguished as before.

5.s:
tato'bravīllubdhakastu brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ tapodhanam .
bhagavan yā tvayā jvālā gṛhotāsīddhutāśanāt .
prayaccha yena mārgāṇi māṃsānyānāyya bhakṣaye .. 5.30 ..
5.d:
ततोऽब्रवील्लुब्धकस्तु ब्राह्मणं तं तपोधनम् ।
भगवन् या त्वया ज्वाला गृहोतासीद्धुताशनात् ।
प्रयच्छ येन मार्गाणि मांसान्यानाय्य भक्षये ॥ 5.30 ॥
5.m: Then the hunter said to that ascetic brāhmaṇa: / "Venerable sir, the flame which was caught by you from the fire, / give it here, so that having brought the deer meat, I may eat it."

5.s:
evamuktastadā vipro yāvadāyasajālakam .
paśyatyeva na tatrāgnirmūlanāśe gataḥ kṣayam .. 5.31 ..
5.d:
एवमुक्तस्तदा विप्रो यावदायसजालकम् ।
पश्यत्येव न तत्राग्निर्मूलनाशे गतः क्षयम् ॥ 5.31 ॥
5.m: Thus addressed, the brāhmaṇa looked as far as the iron mesh; / but the fire was not there, having been destroyed upon the destruction of its root.

5.s:
tato vilakṣabhāvena brāhmaṇaḥ śaṃsitavrataḥ .
tūṣṇīṃbhūtasthitastāvallubdhako vākyamabravīt .. 5.32 ..
5.d:
ततो विलक्षभावेन ब्राह्मणः शंसितव्रतः ।
तूष्णींभूतस्थितस्तावल्लुब्धको वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 5.32 ॥
5.m: Then, as the brāhmaṇa of strict vows remained silent / in an embarrassed state, the hunter spoke these words:

5.s:
etasmiñjvalito vahnirbahuśākhaśca sattama .
mūlanāśe bhavennāśastadvadetadapi dvija .. 5.33 ..
5.d:
एतस्मिञ्ज्वलितो वह्निर्बहुशाखश्च सत्तम ।
मूलनाशे भवेन्नाशस्तद्वदेतदपि द्विज ॥ 5.33 ॥
5.m: "The fire blazed in this [mesh] with many branches, O best of men; / upon the destruction of the root, destruction occurs; just so is this, O twice-born.

5.s: ātmā sa prakṛtisthaśca bhūtānāṃ saṃśrayo bhavet .
5.d: आत्मा स प्रकृतिस्थश्च भूतानां संश्रयो भवेत् ।
5.m:
That Self, abiding in primal nature, becomes the refuge of all beings;
again this creation of the universe takes place right there in that universe.

5.s: bhūya eṣā jagatsṛṣṭistatraiva jagato bhavet .. 5.34 ..
5.d: भूय एषा जगत्सृष्टिस्तत्रैव जगतो भवेत् ॥ 5.34 ॥

5.s:
piṇḍagrahaṇadharmeṇa yadasya vihitaṃ vratam .
tattadātmani saṃyojya kurvāṇo nāvasīdati .. 5.35 ..
5.d:
पिण्डग्रहणधर्मेण यदस्य विहितं व्रतम् ।
तत्तदात्मनि संयोज्य कुर्वाणो नावसीदति ॥ 5.35 ॥
5.m: Whatever vow is prescribed for one by the duty of assuming an embodied form, / offering that very duty up to the self, one who acts does not sink down."

5.s:
evamukte tu vyādhena brāhmaṇe rājasattama .
puṣpavṛṣṭirathākāśāt tasyopari papāta ha .. 5.36 ..
5.d:
एवमुक्ते तु व्याधेन ब्राह्मणे राजसत्तम ।
पुष्पवृष्टिरथाकाशात् तस्योपरि पपात ह ॥ 5.36 ॥
5.m: When this was spoken by the hunter to the brāhmaṇa, O best of kings, / a shower of flowers fell from the sky upon him.

5.s:
vimānāni ca divyāni kāmagāni mahānti ca .
bahuratnāni mukhyāni dadṛśe brāhmaṇottamaḥ .. 5.37 ..
5.d:
विमानानि च दिव्यानि कामगानि महान्ति च ।
बहुरत्नानि मुख्यानि ददृशे ब्राह्मणोत्तमः ॥ 5.37 ॥
5.m: And divine aerial chariots, moving at will, vast, / and adorned with many supreme jewels, the excellent brāhmaṇa beheld.

5.s:
teṣu niṣṭhurakaṃ lubdhaṃ sarveṣu samavasthitam .
dadṛśe brāhmaṇastatra kāmarūpiṇamuttamam .. 5.38 ..
5.d:
तेषु निष्ठुरकं लुब्धं सर्वेषु समवस्थितम् ।
ददृशे ब्राह्मणस्तत्र कामरूपिणमुत्तमम् ॥ 5.38 ॥
5.m: In them, the brāhmaṇa saw the hunter Niṣṭhuraka present in all of them, / capable of assuming forms at will, supreme.

5.s:
advaitavāsanāsiddhaṃ yogād bahuśarīrakam .
dṛṣṭvā vipro mudā yuktaḥ prayayau nijamāśramam .. 5.39 ..
5.d:
अद्वैतवासनासिद्धं योगाद् बहुशरीरकम् ।
दृष्ट्वा विप्रो मुदा युक्तः प्रययौ निजमाश्रमम् ॥ 5.39 ॥
5.m: Seeing him perfected in the impression of non-duality, possessing many bodies through yoga, / the brāhmaṇa, filled with joy, went to his own hermitage.

5.s:
evaṃ jñānavataḥ karmma kurvato'pi svajātikam .
bhavenmuktirdvijaśreṣṭha raibhya rājan vaso dhruvam .. 5.40 ..
5.d:
एवं ज्ञानवतः कर्म्म कुर्वतोऽपि स्वजातिकम् ।
भवेन्मुक्तिर्द्विजश्रेष्ठ रैभ्य राजन् वसो ध्रुवम् ॥ 5.40 ॥
5.m: Thus, even while performing the action proper to his birth, / liberation surely belongs to one endowed with knowledge, O best of the twice-born, O Raibhya, O King Vasu.

5.s:
evaṃ tau saṃśayacchedaṃ prāptau raibhyavasū nṛpa .
bṛhaspatestato dhiṣṇyājjagmaturnijamāśramam .. 5.41 ..
5.d:
एवं तौ संशयच्छेदं प्राप्तौ रैभ्यवसू नृप ।
बृहस्पतेस्ततो धिष्ण्याज्जग्मतुर्निजमाश्रमम् ॥ 5.41 ॥
5.m: Having thus attained the severance of their doubts, Raibhya and Vasu, O king, / then departed from the abode of Bṛhaspati to their own hermitage.

5.s:
tasmāt tvamapi rājendra devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .
abhedena svadehasthaṃ paśyannārādhaya prabhum .. 5.42 ..
5.d:
तस्मात् त्वमपि राजेन्द्र देवं नारायणं प्रभुम् ।
अभेदेन स्वदेहस्थं पश्यन्नाराधय प्रभुम् ॥ 5.42 ॥
5.m: Therefore, O lord of kings, worship the Lord, the god Nārāyaṇa, / seeing the Lord residing within your own body without distinction.

5.s:
kapilasya vacaḥ śrutvā sa rājā'śvaśirā vibhuḥ .
jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ samāhūya dhanyaṃ sthūlaśirāhvayam .
abhiṣicya nije rājye sa rājā prayayau vanam .. 5.43 ..
5.d:
कपिलस्य वचः श्रुत्वा स राजाऽश्वशिरा विभुः ।
ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं समाहूय धन्यं स्थूलशिराह्वयम् ।
अभिषिच्य निजे राज्ये स राजा प्रययौ वनम् ॥ 5.43 ॥
5.m: Hearing the words of Kapila, that powerful king Aśvaśiras, / having summoned his eldest and blessed son named Sthūlaśiras, / and having consecrated him in his own kingdom, departed for the forest.

5.s:
naimiṣākhyaṃ varārohe tatra yajñatanuṃ gurum .
tapasārādhayāmāsa yajñamūrtiṃ stavena ca .. 5.44 ..
5.d:
नैमिषाख्यं वरारोहे तत्र यज्ञतनुं गुरुम् ।
तपसाराधयामास यज्ञमूर्तिं स्तवेन च ॥ 5.44 ॥
5.m: To the place named Naimiṣa, O fair-hipped one; there he worshipped the guru whose body is the sacrifice, / the sacrifice personified, with austerity and praise.

5.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
kathaṃ yajñatanoḥ stotraṃ rājñā nārāyaṇasya ha .
stutiḥ kṛtā mahābhāga punaretacca śaṃsa me .. 5.45 ..
5.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
कथं यज्ञतनोः स्तोत्रं राज्ञा नारायणस्य ह ।
स्तुतिः कृता महाभाग पुनरेतच्च शंस मे ॥ 5.45 ॥
5.m: Dharaṇī said: / How was the praise of Nārāyaṇa, whose body is the sacrifice, / the eulogy uttered by the king? O illustrious one, tell me this again.

5.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
namāmi yājyaṃ tridaśādhipasya
bhavasya sūryasya hutāśanasya .
somasya rājño marutāmaneka-
rūpaṃ hariṃ yajñanaraṃ namasye .. 5.46 ..
5.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
नमामि याज्यं त्रिदशाधिपस्य
भवस्य सूर्यस्य हुताशनस्य ।
सोमस्य राज्ञो मरुतामनेक-
रूपं हरिं यज्ञनरं नमस्ये ॥ 5.46 ॥
5.m: The holy Varāha said: / I bow to the One worthy of sacrifice by the lord of the gods, / by Bhava, by the sun, by the fire, / by King Soma, and by the Maruts; I bow to Hari of manifold / forms, the sacrificial person.

5.s:
subhīmadaṃṣṭraṃ śaśisūryanetraṃ
saṃvatsare cāyanayugmakukṣam .
darbhāṅgaromāṇamathedhmaśaktiṃ
sanātanaṃ yajñanaraṃ namāmi .. 5.47 ..
5.d:
सुभीमदंष्ट्रं शशिसूर्यनेत्रं
संवत्सरे चायनयुग्मकुक्षम् ।
दर्भाङ्गरोमाणमथेध्मशक्तिं
सनातनं यज्ञनरं नमामि ॥ 5.47 ॥
5.m: Having terrible tusks, with the moon and sun as eyes, / with the two solstices as his belly in the year, / having darbha grass as body hair, endowed with the power of sacrificial fuel, / I bow to the eternal sacrificial person.

5.s:
dyāvāpṛthivyoridamantaraṃ hi
vyāptaṃ śarīreṇa diśaśca sarvāḥ .
tamīḍyamīśaṃ jagatāṃ prasūtiṃ
janārdanaṃ taṃ praṇato'smi nityam .. 5.48 ..
5.d:
द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि
व्याप्तं शरीरेण दिशश्च सर्वाः ।
तमीड्यमीशं जगतां प्रसूतिं
जनार्दनं तं प्रणतोऽस्मि नित्यम् ॥ 5.48 ॥
5.m: Indeed, this intermediate space between heaven and earth / and all directions are pervaded by his body. / To that praiseworthy Lord, the origin of the worlds, / to that Janārdana, I am perpetually bowed.

5.s:
surāsurāṇāṃ ca jayājayāya
yuge yuge yaḥ svaśarīramādyam .
sṛjatyanādiḥ parameśvaro ya-
staṃ yajñamūrtiṃ praṇato'smi nātham .. 5.49 ..
5.d:
सुरासुराणां च जयाजयाय
युगे युगे यः स्वशरीरमाद्यम् ।
सृजत्यनादिः परमेश्वरो य-
स्तं यज्ञमूर्तिं प्रणतोऽस्मि नाथम् ॥ 5.49 ॥
5.m: For the victory and defeat of the gods and asuras, / age after age, he who creates his primordial body, / the beginningless, supreme Lord— / to that master whose form is the sacrifice, I am bowed.

5.s:
dadhāra māyāmayamugratejā
jayāya cakraṃ tvamalāṃśuśubhram .
gadāsiśārṅgādicaturbhujo'yaṃ
taṃ yajñamūrtiṃ praṇato'smi nityam .. 5.50 ..
5.d:
दधार मायामयमुग्रतेजा
जयाय चक्रं त्वमलांशुशुभ्रम् ।
गदासिशार्ङ्गादिचतुर्भुजोऽयं
तं यज्ञमूर्तिं प्रणतोऽस्मि नित्यम् ॥ 5.50 ॥
5.m: He of fierce splendor bore the discus composed of māyā, / shining with spotless radiance, for the sake of victory; / this four-armed one holding mace, sword, the Śārṅga bow, and other [weapons]— / to that form of the sacrifice, I am perpetually bowed.

5.s:
kvacit sahastraṃ śirasāṃ dadhāra
kvacinmahāparvatatulyakāyam .
kvacit sa eva trasareṇutulyo
yastaṃ sadā yajñanaraṃ namāmi .. 5.51 ..
5.d:
क्वचित् सहस्त्रं शिरसां दधार
क्वचिन्महापर्वततुल्यकायम् ।
क्वचित् स एव त्रसरेणुतुल्यो
यस्तं सदा यज्ञनरं नमामि ॥ 5.51 ॥
5.m: In one place he bore a thousand heads; / in another, a body equal to a great mountain; / in another, he is equal to a speck of dust in a beam of light— / to that sacrificial person, I ever bow.

5.s:
caturmukho yaḥ sṛjate samagraṃ
rathāṅgapāṇiḥ pratipālanāya .
kṣayāya kālānalasannibho ya-
staṃ yajñamūrtiṃ praṇato'smi nityam .. 5.52 ..
5.d:
चतुर्मुखो यः सृजते समग्रं
रथाङ्गपाणिः प्रतिपालनाय ।
क्षयाय कालानलसन्निभो य-
स्तं यज्ञमूर्तिं प्रणतोऽस्मि नित्यम् ॥ 5.52 ॥
5.m: He who, four-faced, creates the universe, / holding a discus in his hand for its preservation, / and who is like the fire of time for its destruction— / to that form of the sacrifice, I am perpetually bowed.

5.s:
saṃsāracakrakramaṇakriyāyai
ya ijyate sarvagataḥ purāṇaḥ .
yo yogibhirdhyāyate cāprameyas
taṃ yajñamūrtiṃ praṇato'smi nityam .. 5.53 ..
5.d:
संसारचक्रक्रमणक्रियायै
य इज्यते सर्वगतः पुराणः ।
यो योगिभिर्ध्यायते चाप्रमेयस्
तं यज्ञमूर्तिं प्रणतोऽस्मि नित्यम् ॥ 5.53 ॥
5.m: For the operation of the revolving cycle of saṃsāra, / he, all-pervading and ancient, is worshipped with sacrifices; / he who is meditated upon by yogins, immeasurable— / to that form of the sacrifice, I am perpetually bowed.

5.s:
samyaṅmanasyarpitavānahaṃ te
yadā sudṛśyaṃ svatanau nu tattvam .
na cānyadastoti matiḥ sthirā me
yatastato māvatu śuddhabhāvam .. 5.54 ..
5.d:
सम्यङ्मनस्यर्पितवानहं ते
यदा सुदृश्यं स्वतनौ नु तत्त्वम् ।
न चान्यदस्तोति मतिः स्थिरा मे
यतस्ततो मावतु शुद्धभावम् ॥ 5.54 ॥
5.m: Since I have properly deposited in my mind / the truth clearly visible in your body, / and my intellect is steady, knowing there is nothing else, / therefore may you protect me, whose disposition is pure.

5.s:
itīritastasya hutāśanārciḥ -
prakhyaṃ tu tejaḥ purato babhūva .
tasmin sa rājā praviveśa buddhiṃ
kṛtvā layaṃ prāptavān yajñamūrtau .. 5.55 ..
5.d:
इतीरितस्तस्य हुताशनार्चिः -
प्रख्यं तु तेजः पुरतो बभूव ।
तस्मिन् स राजा प्रविवेश बुद्धिं
कृत्वा लयं प्राप्तवान् यज्ञमूर्तौ ॥ 5.55 ॥
5.m: Addressed thus by him, a splendor resembling the flame of fire / appeared before him. / Fixing his intellect upon it, the king entered it / and attained dissolution in the embodiment of sacrifice.

5.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 5 ..
5.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे पञ्चमोऽध्यायः ॥ 5 ॥
5.m: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the holy Varāhapurāṇa, a venerable treatise.

6.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
sa vasuḥ saṃśayacchedaṃ prāpya raibhyaśca sattamaḥ .
ubhau kiṃ cakraturdeva śrutvā cāṅgirasaṃ vacaḥ .. 6.1 ..
6.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
स वसुः संशयच्छेदं प्राप्य रैभ्यश्च सत्तमः ।
उभौ किं चक्रतुर्देव श्रुत्वा चाङ्गिरसं वचः ॥ 6.1 ॥
6.m: Dharaṇī said: / Having had their doubts resolved, what did Vasu / and the best of men, Raibhya, do, O God, / after hearing the words of the descendant of Aṅgiras?

6.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
sa vasuḥ sarvadharmajñaḥ svarājyaṃ pratipālayan .
ayajad bahubhiryajñairmahadbhirbhūridakṣiṇaiḥ .. 6.2 ..
6.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
स वसुः सर्वधर्मज्ञः स्वराज्यं प्रतिपालयन् ।
अयजद् बहुभिर्यज्ञैर्महद्भिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः ॥ 6.2 ॥
6.m: The holy Varāha said: / Vasu, knowing all dharma, ruling his kingdom, / sacrificed with many great sacrifices accompanied by generous fees.

6.s:
karmakāṇḍena deveśaṃ hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .
toṣayāmāsa rājendrastamabhedena cintayan .. 6.3 ..
6.d:
कर्मकाण्डेन देवेशं हरिं नारायणं प्रभुम् ।
तोषयामास राजेन्द्रस्तमभेदेन चिन्तयन् ॥ 6.3 ॥
6.m: By means of the ritual portion, the king of kings pleased / the lord of gods, Hari, Lord Nārāyaṇa, / contemplating him as non-different [from himself].

6.s:
tataḥ kālena mahatā tasya rājño matiḥ kila .
nivṛttarājyabhogasya dndvasyāntamupeyuṣī .. 6.4 ..
6.d:
ततः कालेन महता तस्य राज्ञो मतिः किल ।
निवृत्तराज्यभोगस्य द्न्द्वस्यान्तमुपेयुषी ॥ 6.4 ॥
6.m: Then, after a long time, the intellect of that king / who had renounced the pleasures of kingship, / reached the end of duality.

6.s:
tataḥ putraṃ vivasvantaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhrātṛśatasya ha .
abhiṣicya svake rājye tapovanamupāgamat .. 6.5 ..
6.d:
ततः पुत्रं विवस्वन्तं श्रेष्ठं भ्रातृशतस्य ह ।
अभिषिच्य स्वके राज्ये तपोवनमुपागमत् ॥ 6.5 ॥
6.m: Then, having consecrated in his kingdom / his son Vivasvat, the foremost among a hundred brothers, / he departed for the penance grove.

6.s:
puṣkaraṃ nāma tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ yatra keśavaḥ .
puṇḍarīkākṣanāmā tu pūjyate tatparāyaṇaiḥ .. 6.6 ..
6.d:
पुष्करं नाम तीर्थानां प्रवरं यत्र केशवः ।
पुण्डरीकाक्षनामा तु पूज्यते तत्परायणैः ॥ 6.6 ॥
6.m: He went to Puṣkara, the best of sacred sites, where Keśava, / under the name Puṇḍarīkākṣa, / is worshiped by those devoted to him.

6.s:
tatra gatvā sa rājarṣiḥ kāśmīrādhipatirvasuḥ .
atitīvreṇa tapasā svaśarīramaśoṣayat .. 6.7 ..
6.d:
तत्र गत्वा स राजर्षिः काश्मीराधिपतिर्वसुः ।
अतितीव्रेण तपसा स्वशरीरमशोषयत् ॥ 6.7 ॥
6.m: Going there, that royal sage Vasu, ruler of Kāśmīra, / dried up his body with exceedingly severe austerity.

6.s:
puṇḍarīkākṣapāraṃ tu stavaṃ bhaktyā japan budhaḥ .
ārirādhayiṣurdevaṃ nārāyaṇamakalmaṣam .
stotrānte tallayaṃ prāptaḥ sa rājā rājasattamaḥ .. 6.8 ..
6.d:
पुण्डरीकाक्षपारं तु स्तवं भक्त्या जपन् बुधः ।
आरिराधयिषुर्देवं नारायणमकल्मषम् ।
स्तोत्रान्ते तल्लयं प्राप्तः स राजा राजसत्तमः ॥ 6.8 ॥
6.m: Reciting with devotion the hymn Puṇḍarīkākṣapāra, the wise one / desired to worship the spotless god Nārāyaṇa. / At the end of the praise, that king, best among kings, attained dissolution in him.

6.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
puṇḍarīkākṣapāraṃ tu stotraṃ deva kathaṃ smṛtam .
kīdṛśaṃ tanmamācakṣva parameśvara tattvataḥ .. 6.9 ..
6.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
पुण्डरीकाक्षपारं तु स्तोत्रं देव कथं स्मृतम् ।
कीदृशं तन्ममाचक्ष्व परमेश्वर तत्त्वतः ॥ 6.9 ॥
6.m: Dharaṇī said: / How is the hymn Puṇḍarīkākṣapāra remembered, O God? / What is it like? Explain that to me in truth, O Supreme Lord.

6.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
namaste puṇḍarīkākṣa namaste madhusūdana .
namaste sarvalokeśa namaste tigmacakriṇe .. 6.10 ..
6.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
नमस्ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष नमस्ते मधुसूदन ।
नमस्ते सर्वलोकेश नमस्ते तिग्मचक्रिणे ॥ 6.10 ॥
6.m: The holy Varāha said: / Salutation to you, O Lotus-Eyed! Salutation to you, O Madhusūdana! / Salutation to you, O Lord of all worlds! Salutation to you, bearer of the sharp discus!

6.s:
viśvamūrtiṃ mahābāhuṃ varadaṃ sarvatejasam .
namāmi puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ vidyā'vidyātmakaṃ vibhum .. 6.11 ..
6.d:
विश्वमूर्तिं महाबाहुं वरदं सर्वतेजसम् ।
नमामि पुण्डरीकाक्षं विद्याऽविद्यात्मकं विभुम् ॥ 6.11 ॥
6.m: I bow to the Lotus-Eyed, the embodiment of the universe, mighty-armed, / the granter of boons, all-luminous, the omnipresent whose nature is knowledge and ignorance.

6.s:
ādidevaṃ mahādevaṃ vedavedāṅgapāragam .
gambhīraṃ sarvadevānāṃ namāmi madhusūdanam .. 6.12 ..
6.d:
आदिदेवं महादेवं वेदवेदाङ्गपारगम् ।
गम्भीरं सर्वदेवानां नमामि मधुसूदनम् ॥ 6.12 ॥
6.m: I bow to Madhusūdana, the primal god, the great god, / who has crossed to the further shore of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / the unfathomable one of all gods.

6.s:
viśvamūrtiṃ mahāmūrtiṃ vidyāmūrtiṃ trimūrtikam .
kavacaṃ sarvadevānāṃ namasye vārijekṣaṇam .. 6.13 ..
6.d:
विश्वमूर्तिं महामूर्तिं विद्यामूर्तिं त्रिमूर्तिकम् ।
कवचं सर्वदेवानां नमस्ये वारिजेक्षणम् ॥ 6.13 ॥
6.m: I revere the lotus-eyed one, the embodiment of the universe, the great embodiment, / the embodiment of knowledge, having three forms, / the armor of all gods.

6.s:
sahastraśīrṣiṇaṃ devaṃ sahastrākṣaṃ mahābhujam .
jagatsaṃvyāpya tiṣṭhantaṃ namasye parameśvaram .. 6.14 ..
6.d:
सहस्त्रशीर्षिणं देवं सहस्त्राक्षं महाभुजम् ।
जगत्संव्याप्य तिष्ठन्तं नमस्ये परमेश्वरम् ॥ 6.14 ॥
6.m: I revere the Supreme Lord, the god with a thousand heads, / a thousand eyes, and mighty arms, / who stands pervading the world.

6.s:
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ devaṃ viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ sanātanam .
nīlameghapratīkāśaṃ namasye cakrapāṇinam .. 6.15 ..
6.d:
शरण्यं शरणं देवं विष्णुं जिष्णुं सनातनम् ।
नीलमेघप्रतीकाशं नमस्ये चक्रपाणिनम् ॥ 6.15 ॥
6.m: I revere the holder of the discus, refuge of the seekers of refuge, / the god Viṣṇu, victorious, eternal, / who resembles a dark rain-cloud.

6.s:
śuddhaṃ sarvagataṃ nityaṃ vyomarūpaṃ sanātanam .
bhāvābhāvavinirmuktaṃ masye sarvagaṃ harim .. 6.16 ..
6.d:
शुद्धं सर्वगतं नित्यं व्योमरूपं सनातनम् ।
भावाभावविनिर्मुक्तं मस्ये सर्वगं हरिम् ॥ 6.16 ॥
6.m: I revere Hari, pure, all-pervading, eternal, / having the form of ether, everlasting, / free from existence and non-existence, going everywhere.

6.s:
nānyat kiṃcit prapaśyāmi vyatiriktaṃ tvayā'cyuta .
tvanmayaṃ ca prapaśyāmi sarvametaccarācaram .. 6.17 ..
6.d:
नान्यत् किंचित् प्रपश्यामि व्यतिरिक्तं त्वयाऽच्युत ।
त्वन्मयं च प्रपश्यामि सर्वमेतच्चराचरम् ॥ 6.17 ॥
6.m: I see nothing whatever separate from you, O Acyuta, / and I see this entire world of moving and unmoving beings consisting of you.

6.s:
evaṃ tu vadatastasya mūrttimān puruṣaḥ kila .
nirgatya dehānnīlābho ghanacaṇḍo bhayaṃkaraḥ .. 6.18 ..
6.d:
एवं तु वदतस्तस्य मूर्त्तिमान् पुरुषः किल ।
निर्गत्य देहान्नीलाभो घनचण्डो भयंकरः ॥ 6.18 ॥
6.m: While he was speaking thus, an embodied man, / having the luster of dark blue, fierce like a rain-cloud, and terrifying, / came forth from his body.

6.s:
raktākṣo hrasvakāyastu dagdhasthūṇāsamaprabhaḥ .
uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā kiṃ karomi narādhipa .. 6.19 ..
6.d:
रक्ताक्षो ह्रस्वकायस्तु दग्धस्थूणासमप्रभः ।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा किं करोमि नराधिप ॥ 6.19 ॥
6.m: Red-eyed, short of stature, / with a luster like a burnt pillar, / he folded his hands and said: “What shall I do, O ruler of men?”

6.s:
rājovāca .
ko'si kiṃ kāryamiha te kasmādāgatavānasi .
etanme kathaya vyādha etadicchāmi veditum .. 6.20 ..
6.d:
राजोवाच ।
कोऽसि किं कार्यमिह ते कस्मादागतवानसि ।
एतन्मे कथय व्याध एतदिच्छामि वेदितुम् ॥ 6.20 ॥
6.m: The king said: / “Who are you? What is your business here? Whence have you come? / Tell me this, O hunter; this I wish to know.”

6.s:
vyādha uvāca .
pūrvaṃ kaliyuge rājan rājā tvaṃ dakṣiṇāpathe .
pūrṇadharmodbhavaḥ śrīmāñjanasthāne vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 6.21 ..
6.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
पूर्वं कलियुगे राजन् राजा त्वं दक्षिणापथे ।
पूर्णधर्मोद्भवः श्रीमाञ्जनस्थाने विचक्षणः ॥ 6.21 ॥
6.m: The hunter said: / “Formerly in the Kali yuga, O King, you were a king in the south, / born of full righteousness, glorious, and wise, in Janasthāna.

6.s:
sa kadācid bhavān vīra turagaiḥ parivāritaḥ .
araṇyamāgato hantuṃ śvāpadāni viśeṣataḥ .. 6.22 ..
6.d:
स कदाचिद् भवान् वीर तुरगैः परिवारितः ।
अरण्यमागतो हन्तुं श्वापदानि विशेषतः ॥ 6.22 ॥
6.m: Once, O hero, surrounded by horses, / you entered the forest to hunt wild beasts in particular.

6.s:
tatra tvayā'nyakāmena mṛgaveṣadharo muniḥ .
daṇḍayugmena dūre tu pātito dharaṇītale .. 6.23 ..
6.d:
तत्र त्वयाऽन्यकामेन मृगवेषधरो मुनिः ।
दण्डयुग्मेन दूरे तु पातितो धरणीतले ॥ 6.23 ॥
6.m: There, having another intent, you felled to the surface of the earth from afar / with two arrows a sage wearing the guise of a deer.

6.s:
sadyo mṛtaśca viprendrastvaṃ ca rājan mudā yutaḥ .
hariṇo'yaṃ hata iti yāvat paśyasi pārthiva .
6.d:
सद्यो मृतश्च विप्रेन्द्रस्त्वं च राजन् मुदा युतः ।
हरिणोऽयं हत इति यावत् पश्यसि पार्थिव ।

6.s: tāvanmṛgavapurvipro mṛtaḥ prastravaṇe girau .. 6.24 ..
6.d: तावन्मृगवपुर्विप्रो मृतः प्रस्त्रवणे गिरौ ॥ 6.24 ॥

6.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā tvaṃ mahārāja kṣubhitendriyamānasaḥ .
gṛhaṃ gatastato'nyasya kasyacit kathitaṃ tvayā .. 6.25 ..
6.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा त्वं महाराज क्षुभितेन्द्रियमानसः ।
गृहं गतस्ततोऽन्यस्य कस्यचित् कथितं त्वया ॥ 6.25 ॥
6.m: Seeing him, your mind and senses agitated, O great king, / you went home, and then told another.

6.s:
tataḥ katipayāhasya tvayā rātrau nareśvara .
brahmahatyābhayādbhītacitenaitad vicintitam .
kṛtyaṃ karomi śāntyarthaṃ mucyate yena pātakāt .. 6.26 ..
6.d:
ततः कतिपयाहस्य त्वया रात्रौ नरेश्वर ।
ब्रह्महत्याभयाद्भीतचितेनैतद् विचिन्तितम् ।
कृत्यं करोमि शान्त्यर्थं मुच्यते येन पातकात् ॥ 6.26 ॥
6.m: Then, some days later, at night, O ruler of men, / your mind was terrified by fear of the killing of a brāhmaṇa, and you thought: / ‘What deed shall I do for pacification, whereby I may be freed from sin?’

6.s:
tatastvayā mahārāja sakṛnnārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .
saṃcintya dvādaśī śuddhā tvayā rājannupoṣitā .. 6.27 ..
6.d:
ततस्त्वया महाराज सकृन्नारायणं प्रभुम् ।
संचिन्त्य द्वादशी शुद्धा त्वया राजन्नुपोषिता ॥ 6.27 ॥
6.m: Then, O great king, having contemplated Lord Nārāyaṇa once, / you observed a fast on the pure Dvādaśī, O King.

6.s:
nārāyaṇo me suprīta iti proktvā śubhe'hani .
gaurdattā vidhinā sadyo mṛto'syudaraśūlataḥ .. 6.28 ..
6.d:
नारायणो मे सुप्रीत इति प्रोक्त्वा शुभेऽहनि ।
गौर्दत्ता विधिना सद्यो मृतोऽस्युदरशूलतः ॥ 6.28 ॥
6.m: Saying on that auspicious day, ‘May Nārāyaṇa be well pleased with me,’ / a cow was given according to rule; and immediately you died of colic.

6.s:
abhukto dvādaśīdharme yat tatrāpi ca kāraṇam .
kathayāmi bhavatpatnī nāmnā nārāyaṇī śubhā .. 6.29 ..
6.d:
अभुक्तो द्वादशीधर्मे यत् तत्रापि च कारणम् ।
कथयामि भवत्पत्नी नाम्ना नारायणी शुभा ॥ 6.29 ॥
6.m: Because you did not break the fast according to the rule of Dvādaśī, / I shall tell you the reason: your auspicious wife, named Nārāyaṇī,

6.s:
sā kaṇṭhagena prāṇena vyāhṛtā tena te gatiḥ .
kalpamekaṃ mahārāja jātā viṣṇupure tava .. 6.30 ..
6.d:
सा कण्ठगेन प्राणेन व्याहृता तेन ते गतिः ।
कल्पमेकं महाराज जाता विष्णुपुरे तव ॥ 6.30 ॥
6.m: called out to you as life was in your throat; by that, O great king, / your destination for one kalpa became the city of Viṣṇu.

6.s:
ahaṃ ca tava dehasthaḥ sarvaṃ jānāmi cākṣayam .
brahmagraho mahāghoraḥ pīḍayāmīti me matiḥ .. 6.31 ..
6.d:
अहं च तव देहस्थः सर्वं जानामि चाक्षयम् ।
ब्रह्मग्रहो महाघोरः पीडयामीति मे मतिः ॥ 6.31 ॥
6.m: Residing in your body, I knew everything imperishable; / I, the terrible Brahma-graha, thought: ‘I will torment him.’

6.s:
tāvadviṣṇostu puruṣaiḥ kiṅkarairmusalairaham .
prahataḥ saṃkṣayaṃ yātastataste romakūpataḥ .
svargasthasyāpi rājendra sthito'haṃ svena tejasā .. 6.32 ..
6.d:
तावद्विष्णोस्तु पुरुषैः किङ्करैर्मुसलैरहम् ।
प्रहतः संक्षयं यातस्ततस्ते रोमकूपतः ।
स्वर्गस्थस्यापि राजेन्द्र स्थितोऽहं स्वेन तेजसा ॥ 6.32 ॥
6.m: Then, struck with maces by Viṣṇu’s servants, his attendants, / I was reduced to destruction; thence, O king of kings, / I remained through my own energy in the pores of your hair even while you were in heaven.

6.s:
tato'haḥkalpanirvṛtte rātrikalpe ca sattama .
idānīmādisṛṣṭau tu kṛte nṛpatisattama .. 6.33 ..
6.d:
ततोऽहःकल्पनिर्वृत्ते रात्रिकल्पे च सत्तम ।
इदानीमादिसृष्टौ तु कृते नृपतिसत्तम ॥ 6.33 ॥
6.m: Then, when the day-kalpa and the night-kalpa had ended, O best of men, / now at the primal creation, in the Kṛta yuga, O best of kings,

6.s:
saṃbhūtastvaṃ mahārāja rājñaḥ sumanaso gṛhe .
kāśmīradeśādhipaterahaṃ cāṅgaruhaistava .. 6.34 ..
6.d:
संभूतस्त्वं महाराज राज्ञः सुमनसो गृहे ।
काश्मीरदेशाधिपतेरहं चाङ्गरुहैस्तव ॥ 6.34 ॥
6.m: you were born, O great king, in the house of King Sumanas, / ruler of the country of Kāśmīra; and I, through your body-hairs, [came along].

6.s:
yajñairiṣṭaṃ tvayānekairbahubhiścāptadakṣiṇaiḥ .
na cāhaṃ tairapahato viṣṇusmaraṇavarjitaiḥ .. 6.35 ..
6.d:
यज्ञैरिष्टं त्वयानेकैर्बहुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः ।
न चाहं तैरपहतो विष्णुस्मरणवर्जितैः ॥ 6.35 ॥
6.m: You sacrificed with numerous and various sacrifices accompanied by ample fees, / but I was not removed by them, since they lacked remembrance of Viṣṇu.

6.s:
idānīṃ yat tvayā stotraṃ puṇḍarīkākṣapārakam .
paṭhitaṃ tatprabhāvena vihāyāṅgaruhāṇyaham .
ekībhūtaḥ punarjāto vyādharūpo nṛpottama .. 6.36 ..
6.d:
इदानीं यत् त्वया स्तोत्रं पुण्डरीकाक्षपारकम् ।
पठितं तत्प्रभावेन विहायाङ्गरुहाण्यहम् ।
एकीभूतः पुनर्जातो व्याधरूपो नृपोत्तम ॥ 6.36 ॥
6.m: Now, by the power of the hymn Puṇḍarīkākṣapāra / recited by you, leaving the hairs of your body, / I have become unified and born again in the form of a hunter, O best of kings.

6.s:
ahaṃ bhagavataḥ stotraṃ śrutvā prākpāpamūrttinā .
mukto'smi dharmabuddhirme varttate sāmprataṃ vibho .. 6.37 ..
6.d:
अहं भगवतः स्तोत्रं श्रुत्वा प्राक्पापमूर्त्तिना ।
मुक्तोऽस्मि धर्मबुद्धिर्मे वर्त्तते साम्प्रतं विभो ॥ 6.37 ॥
6.m: Having heard the Lord’s hymn, I am freed / from that former form of sin; now a righteous mind dwells in me, O lord.

6.s:
etacchrutvā vaco rājā paraṃ vismayamāgataḥ .
vareṇa chandayāmāsa taṃ vyādhaṃ rājasattamaḥ .. 6.38 ..
6.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो राजा परं विस्मयमागतः ।
वरेण छन्दयामास तं व्याधं राजसत्तमः ॥ 6.38 ॥
6.m: Hearing these words, the king was filled with supreme wonder; / the best of kings offered that hunter a boon.

6.s:
rājovāca .
smārito'smi yathā vyādha tvayā janmāntaraṃ gatam .
tathā tvaṃ matprasādena dharmavyādho bhaviṣyasi .. 6.39 ..
6.d:
राजोवाच ।
स्मारितोऽस्मि यथा व्याध त्वया जन्मान्तरं गतम् ।
तथा त्वं मत्प्रसादेन धर्मव्याधो भविष्यसि ॥ 6.39 ॥
6.m:
The king said:
'Just as, O hunter, I have been reminded by you of my past birth, / so by my favor you shall become Dharmavyādha.'

6.s:
yaścaitat puṇḍarīkākṣapāragaṃ śrṛṇuyāt param .
tasya puṣkarayātrāyāṃ vidhisnānaphalaṃ bhavet .. 6.40 ..
6.d:
यश्चैतत् पुण्डरीकाक्षपारगं श्रृणुयात् परम् ।
तस्य पुष्करयात्रायां विधिस्नानफलं भवेत् ॥ 6.40 ॥
6.m: And whoever hears this supreme [hymn] leading across to the lotus-eyed [Lord], / shall obtain the fruit of a prescribed bath on a pilgrimage to Puṣkara.

6.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
evamuktvā tato rājā vimānavaramāsthitaḥ .
pareṇa tejasā yogamavāpāśeṣadhāriṇi .. 6.41 ..
6.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजा विमानवरमास्थितः ।
परेण तेजसा योगमवापाशेषधारिणि ॥ 6.41 ॥
6.m:
Śrī Varāha said:
Having spoken thus, the king, seated on an excellent aerial chariot, / attained union [with the Lord] through supreme splendor, O bearer of all!

6.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ .. 6 ..
6.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे षष्ठोऽध्यायः ॥ 6 ॥
6.m: Thus ends the sixth chapter in the holy Varāhapurāṇa, the scripture of the Lord.

7.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
raibhyo'sau muniśārdūlaḥ śrutvā siddhaṃ vasuṃ tadā .
svayaṃ kimakarod deva saṃśayo me mahānayam .. 7.1 ..
7.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
रैभ्योऽसौ मुनिशार्दूलः श्रुत्वा सिद्धं वसुं तदा ।
स्वयं किमकरोद् देव संशयो मे महानयम् ॥ 7.1 ॥
7.m:
Dharaṇī said:
'What did that sage Raibhya, best among munis, do himself, / having heard that Vasu had attained spiritual accomplishment, O Lord? This is my great doubt.'

7.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
sa raibhyo muniśārdūlaḥ śrutvā siddhaṃ vasuṃ tadā .
ājagāma gayāṃ puṇyāṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ tapodhanaḥ .
tatra gatvā pitṝn bhaktyā piṇḍadānena tarpayat .. 7.2 ..
7.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
स रैभ्यो मुनिशार्दूलः श्रुत्वा सिद्धं वसुं तदा ।
आजगाम गयां पुण्यां पितृतीर्थं तपोधनः ।
तत्र गत्वा पितॄन् भक्त्या पिण्डदानेन तर्पयत् ॥ 7.2 ॥
7.m:
Śrī Varāha said:
Having heard that Vasu had then attained spiritual accomplishment, that Raibhya, best among munis, rich in asceticism, / came to sacred Gayā, the pilgrimage place of the ancestors. / Having gone there, he gratified the ancestors with devotion by offering rice balls.

7.s:
tato vai suhamattīvraṃ tapaḥ paramaduścaram .
caratastasya tattīvraṃ tapo raibhyasya dhīmataḥ .
ājagāma mahāyogī vimānastho'tidīptimān .. 7.3 ..
7.d:
ततो वै सुहमत्तीव्रं तपः परमदुश्चरम् ।
चरतस्तस्य तत्तीव्रं तपो रैभ्यस्य धीमतः ।
आजगाम महायोगी विमानस्थोऽतिदीप्तिमान् ॥ 7.3 ॥
7.m: Then indeed he [undertook] very fierce and extremely arduous asceticism. / As wise Raibhya was practicing that fierce asceticism, / a great yogin, exceedingly radiant, arrived seated in an aerial chariot.

7.s:
trasareṇusame śuddhe vimāne sūryasannibhe .
paramāṇupramāṇena puruṣastatra dīptimān .. 7.4 ..
7.d:
त्रसरेणुसमे शुद्धे विमाने सूर्यसन्निभे ।
परमाणुप्रमाणेन पुरुषस्तत्र दीप्तिमान् ॥ 7.4 ॥
7.m: In a pure aerial chariot equal to a speck of dust, resembling the sun, / was a radiant person the size of an atom.

7.s:
so'bravīd raibhya kiṃ kāryaṃ tapaścarasi suvrata .
evamuktvā divo bhūmiṃ māpayāmāsa vai pumān .. 7.5 ..
7.d:
सोऽब्रवीद् रैभ्य किं कार्यं तपश्चरसि सुव्रत ।
एवमुक्त्वा दिवो भूमिं मापयामास वै पुमान् ॥ 7.5 ॥
7.m: He said: 'O Raibhya of good vows, for what purpose do you practice asceticism?' / Having spoken thus, that person measured the earth from heaven.

7.s:
tatrāpi rathapañcābhaṃ vimānaṃ sūryasannibham .
yugapad brahmabhuvanaṃ vyāpnuvantaṃ dadarśa saḥ .. 7.6 ..
7.d:
तत्रापि रथपञ्चाभं विमानं सूर्यसन्निभम् ।
युगपद् ब्रह्मभुवनं व्याप्नुवन्तं ददर्श सः ॥ 7.6 ॥
7.m: There he also saw an aerial chariot resembling the sun, having the luster of five chariots, / simultaneously pervading the world of Brahmā.

7.s:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo raibhyaḥ praṇatipūrvakam .
papraccha taṃ mahāyogin ko bhavān prabravītu me .. 7.7 ..
7.d:
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो रैभ्यः प्रणतिपूर्वकम् ।
पप्रच्छ तं महायोगिन् को भवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥ 7.7 ॥
7.m: Filled with wonder, Raibhya bowed before him / and asked: 'O great yogin, tell me, who are you?'

7.s:
puruṣa uvāca .
ahaṃ rudrādavarajo brahmaṇo mānasaḥ sutaḥ .
nāmnā sanatkumāreti janaloke vasāmyaham .. 7.8 ..
7.d:
पुरुष उवाच ।
अहं रुद्रादवरजो ब्रह्मणो मानसः सुतः ।
नाम्ना सनत्कुमारेति जनलोके वसाम्यहम् ॥ 7.8 ॥
7.m:
The Person said:
'I am the younger brother of Rudra, the mind-born son of Brahmā, / named Sanatkumāra; I dwell in Janaloka.

7.s:
bhavataḥ pārśvamāyātaḥ praṇayena tapodhana .
dhanyo'si sarvathā vatsa brahmaṇaḥ kulavardhanaḥ .. 7.9 ..
7.d:
भवतः पार्श्वमायातः प्रणयेन तपोधन ।
धन्योऽसि सर्वथा वत्स ब्रह्मणः कुलवर्धनः ॥ 7.9 ॥
7.m: I have come to your side out of affection, O rich in asceticism. / You are blessed in every way, my child, an increaser of the family of Brahmā.'

7.s:
raibhya uvāca .
namo'stu te yogivara prasīda
dayāṃ mahyaṃ kuruṣe viśvarūpa .
kimatra kṛtyaṃ vada yogisiṃha
kathaṃ hi dhanyo'hamuktastvayā ca .. 7.10 ..
7.d:
रैभ्य उवाच ।
नमोऽस्तु ते योगिवर प्रसीद
दयां मह्यं कुरुषे विश्वरूप ।
किमत्र कृत्यं वद योगिसिंह
कथं हि धन्योऽहमुक्तस्त्वया च ॥ 7.10 ॥
7.m:
Raibhya said:
'Obeisance to you, best of yogins! Be gracious, / grant me compassion, O you whose form is the universe! / Tell me, O lion among yogins, what should be done here? / And why have you spoken of me as blessed?'

7.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca .
dhanyastvameva dvijavaryamukhya
yad vedavādābhirataḥ pitṝṃśca .
prīṇāsi mantravratajapyahomai-
rgayāṃ samāsādya tathā'nnapiṇḍaiḥ .. 7.11 ..
7.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
धन्यस्त्वमेव द्विजवर्यमुख्य
यद् वेदवादाभिरतः पितॄंश्च ।
प्रीणासि मन्त्रव्रतजप्यहोमै-
र्गयां समासाद्य तथाऽन्नपिण्डैः ॥ 7.11 ॥
7.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
'Blessed indeed are you, foremost of the best of the twice-born, / since, devoted to the declarations of the Veda, you satisfy the ancestors / with mantras, vows, muttered prayers, and oblations into fire, / as well as with rice balls of food after reaching Gayā.

7.s:
śrṛṇuṣva cānyaṃ nṛpatirbabhūva
viśālanāmā sa purīṃ viśālām .
uvāsa dhanyo dhṛtimānaputraḥ
svayaṃ viśālādhipatirdvijāgryān .
papraccha putrārthamamitrasāha -
ste brāhmaṇāścocuradīnasattvāḥ .. 7.12 ..
7.d:
श्रृणुष्व चान्यं नृपतिर्बभूव
विशालनामा स पुरीं विशालाम् ।
उवास धन्यो धृतिमानपुत्रः
स्वयं विशालाधिपतिर्द्विजाग्र्यान् ।
पप्रच्छ पुत्रार्थममित्रसाह -
स्ते ब्राह्मणाश्चोचुरदीनसत्त्वाः ॥ 7.12 ॥
7.m: Hear also another [story]. There was a king / named Viśāla; he dwelt in the city of Viśālā. / Blessed, resolute, but sonless, / the lord of Viśālā himself, vanquisher of foes, / asked the foremost among the twice-born for the sake of a son; and those brāhmaṇas of noble nature said:

7.s:
rgatvā gayāmannadānairanekaiḥ .
dhruvaṃ sutaste bhavitā nṛpeśa
susaṃpradātā sakalakṣitīśaḥ .. 7.13 ..
7.d:
र्गत्वा गयामन्नदानैरनेकैः ।
ध्रुवं सुतस्ते भविता नृपेश
सुसंप्रदाता सकलक्षितीशः ॥ 7.13 ॥
7.m: '[...by going to] Gayā with many gifts of food, / a son will surely be born to you, O lord of kings, / a generous giver and king of the entire earth.'

7.s:
itīrito brāhmaṇaiḥ sa prahṛṣṭo
rājā viśālādhipatiḥ prayatnāt .
āgatya tena pravareṇa tīrthe
maghāsu bhaktyā'tha kṛtaṃ pitṝṇām .. 7.14 ..
7.d:
इतीरितो ब्राह्मणैः स प्रहृष्टो
राजा विशालाधिपतिः प्रयत्नात् ।
आगत्य तेन प्रवरेण तीर्थे
मघासु भक्त्याऽथ कृतं पितॄणाम् ॥ 7.14 ॥
7.m: Thus addressed by the brāhmaṇas, that king, the lord of Viśālā, delighted, / came with diligence to that excellent sacred place / during the Maghā constellation, and with devotion performed for the ancestors

7.s:
piṇḍapradānaṃ vidhinā prayatnā-
dadadviyatyuttamamūrtayastān .
paśyan sa puṃsaḥ sitapītakṛṣṇā-
nuvāca rājā kimidaṃ bhavadbhiḥ .
upekṣyate śaṃsata sarvameva
kautūhalaṃ me manasi pravṛttam .. 7.15 ..
7.d:
पिण्डप्रदानं विधिना प्रयत्ना-
ददद्वियत्युत्तममूर्तयस्तान् ।
पश्यन् स पुंसः सितपीतकृष्णा-
नुवाच राजा किमिदं भवद्भिः ।
उपेक्ष्यते शंसत सर्वमेव
कौतूहलं मे मनसि प्रवृत्तम् ॥ 7.15 ॥
7.m: the offering of rice balls with diligence according to rule. / Seeing in the sky those persons of excellent forms, white, yellow, and black, / the king said: 'Why is this neglected by you? / Tell me everything; curiosity has arisen in my mind.'

7.s:
sita uvāca .
ahaṃ sitaste janako'smi tāta
nāmnā ca vṛttena ca karmaṇā ca .
ayaṃ ca me janako raktavarṇo
nṛśaṃsakṛd brahmahā pāpakārī .. 7.16 ..
7.d:
सित उवाच ।
अहं सितस्ते जनकोऽस्मि तात
नाम्ना च वृत्तेन च कर्मणा च ।
अयं च मे जनको रक्तवर्णो
नृशंसकृद् ब्रह्महा पापकारी ॥ 7.16 ॥
7.m:
The white one said:
'I, the white one, am your father, my son, / by name, conduct, and deeds. / And this red-colored one is my father, / a perpetrator of cruelty, a slayer of brāhmaṇas, an evildoer.

7.s:
adhīśvaro nāma paraḥ pitā'sya
kṛṣṇo vṛttyā karmaṇā cāpi kṛṣṇaḥ .
etena kṛṣṇena hatāḥ purā vai
janmanyaneke ṛṣayaḥ purāṇāḥ .. 7.17 ..
7.d:
अधीश्वरो नाम परः पिताऽस्य
कृष्णो वृत्त्या कर्मणा चापि कृष्णः ।
एतेन कृष्णेन हताः पुरा वै
जन्मन्यनेके ऋषयः पुराणाः ॥ 7.17 ॥
7.m: The father beyond him, named Adhīśvara, / is black—black in conduct and also in deeds. / By this black one, in past times indeed, / many ancient ṛṣis were killed in [his] birth.

7.s:
etau mṛtau dvāvapi putra raudra-
mavīcisaṃjñaṃ narakaṃ prapannau .
adhīśvaro me janakaḥ paro'sya
kṛṣṇaḥ pitā dvāvapi dīrghakālam .
ahaṃ ca śuddhena nijena karmaṇā
śakrāsanaṃ prāpito durlabhaṃ tataḥ .. 7.18 ..
7.d:
एतौ मृतौ द्वावपि पुत्र रौद्र-
मवीचिसंज्ञं नरकं प्रपन्नौ ।
अधीश्वरो मे जनकः परोऽस्य
कृष्णः पिता द्वावपि दीर्घकालम् ।
अहं च शुद्धेन निजेन कर्मणा
शक्रासनं प्रापितो दुर्लभं ततः ॥ 7.18 ॥
7.m: Both of them, having died, O son, entered the terrible / hell named Avīci. / Adhīśvara is my grandfather, and the one beyond him, / the black one, is my father's father; both were there for a long time. / And I, by my own pure deeds, / was subsequently brought to the rarely attained seat of Śakra.

7.s:
tvayā punarmantravidā gayāyāṃ
piṇḍapradānena balādimau ca .
melāpitau tīrthapiṇḍapradāna -
prabhāvato me narakāśritāvapi .. 7.19 ..
7.d:
त्वया पुनर्मन्त्रविदा गयायां
पिण्डप्रदानेन बलादिमौ च ।
मेलापितौ तीर्थपिण्डप्रदान -
प्रभावतो मे नरकाश्रितावपि ॥ 7.19 ॥
7.m: Yet by you, a knower of mantras, through the offering of rice balls at Gayā, / these two have also forcibly / been brought together with me by the power of the rice ball offering at the sacred place, though they were dwellers in hell.

7.s:
pitṝn pitāmahāṃstatra tathaiva prapitāmahān .
prīṇayāmīti tattoyaṃ tvayā dattamariṃdama .. 7.20 ..
7.d:
पितॄन् पितामहांस्तत्र तथैव प्रपितामहान् ।
प्रीणयामीति तत्तोयं त्वया दत्तमरिंदम ॥ 7.20 ॥
7.m: "I gratify the fathers, grandfathers, / and likewise the great-grandfathers": saying this, that water was offered by you, O tamer of foes.

7.s:
tenāsmadyugapadyogo jāto vākyena sattama .
tīrthaprabhāvād gacchāmaḥ pitṛlokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 7.21 ..
7.d:
तेनास्मद्युगपद्योगो जातो वाक्येन सत्तम ।
तीर्थप्रभावाद् गच्छामः पितृलोकं न संशयः ॥ 7.21 ॥
7.m: By that statement, O best of men, our simultaneous union occurred. / By the power of the sacred place we go to the world of the ancestors; there is no doubt.

7.s:
atra piṇḍapradānena etau tava pitāmahau .
durgatāvapi saṃsiddhau pāpakṛdvikṛtiṃ gatau .. 7.22 ..
7.d:
अत्र पिण्डप्रदानेन एतौ तव पितामहौ ।
दुर्गतावपि संसिद्धौ पापकृद्विकृतिं गतौ ॥ 7.22 ॥
7.m: Here, by the offering of rice balls, these two ancestors of yours, / though fallen into misfortune and transformed by evil deeds, have attained perfection.

7.s:
tīrthaprabhāva eṣo'smin brahmaghnasyāpi tatsutaḥ .
putaḥ piṇḍapradānena kuryāduddharaṇaṃ punaḥ .. 7.23 ..
7.d:
तीर्थप्रभाव एषोऽस्मिन् ब्रह्मघ्नस्यापि तत्सुतः ।
पुतः पिण्डप्रदानेन कुर्यादुद्धरणं पुनः ॥ 7.23 ॥
7.m: Such is the power of this sacred place: even of a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, the son, / purified, can again effect deliverance by the offering of rice balls.

7.s:
etasmāt kāraṇāt putra ahametau vigṛhya vai .
āgato'smi bhavantaṃ vai draṣṭuṃ yāsyāmi sāmpratam .
etasmāt kāraṇād raibhya bhavān dhanyo mayocyate .. 7.24 ..
7.d:
एतस्मात् कारणात् पुत्र अहमेतौ विगृह्य वै ।
आगतोऽस्मि भवन्तं वै द्रष्टुं यास्यामि साम्प्रतम् ।
एतस्मात् कारणाद् रैभ्य भवान् धन्यो मयोच्यते ॥ 7.24 ॥
7.m: For this reason, O son, taking these two with me, / I have come to see you; now I shall depart. / For this reason, O Raibhya, you are declared blessed by me.

7.s:
sakṛd gayābhigamanaṃ sakṛtpiṇḍapradāpanam .
durlabhaṃ tvaṃ punarnityamasminneva vyavasthitaḥ .. 7.25 ..
7.d:
सकृद् गयाभिगमनं सकृत्पिण्डप्रदापनम् ।
दुर्लभं त्वं पुनर्नित्यमस्मिन्नेव व्यवस्थितः ॥ 7.25 ॥
7.m: Going to Gayā even once, or offering rice balls even once, / is difficult to attain; yet you are constantly established in this very place!

7.s:
kimanu procyate raibhya tava puṇyamidaṃ prabho .
yena sākṣād gadāpāṇirdṛṣṭo nārāyaṇaḥ svayam .. 7.26 ..
7.d:
किमनु प्रोच्यते रैभ्य तव पुण्यमिदं प्रभो ।
येन साक्षाद् गदापाणिर्दृष्टो नारायणः स्वयम् ॥ 7.26 ॥
7.m: How can this merit of yours be fully described, O Raibhya, O lord, / by which Nārāyaṇa himself, holding the mace in his hand, was seen visibly?

7.s:
tato gadādharaḥ sākṣādasmiṃstīrthe vyavasthitaḥ .
ato'tivikhyātatamaṃ tīrthametad dvijottama .. 7.27 ..
7.d:
ततो गदाधरः साक्षादस्मिंस्तीर्थे व्यवस्थितः ।
अतोऽतिविख्याततमं तीर्थमेतद् द्विजोत्तम ॥ 7.27 ॥
7.m: Hence Gadādhara is visibly established at this sacred place; / therefore this sacred place is renowned above all, O best of the twice-born.'

7.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
evamuktvā mahāyogī tatraivāntaradhīyata .
raibhyo'pi ca gadāpāṇerhareḥ stotramathākarot .. 7.28 ..
7.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा महायोगी तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।
रैभ्योऽपि च गदापाणेर्हरेः स्तोत्रमथाकरोत् ॥ 7.28 ॥
7.m:
Śrī Varāha said:
Having spoken thus, the great yogin vanished right there. / Raibhya, too, then offered praise to Hari, who holds the mace in his hand.

7.s:
raibhya uvāca .
gadādharaṃ vibudhajanairabhiṣṭutaṃ
dhṛtakṣamaṃ kṣudhitajanārttināśanam .
śivaṃ viśālāsurasainyamardanaṃ
namāmyahaṃ hatasakalāśubhaṃ smṛtau .. 7.29 ..
7.d:
रैभ्य उवाच ।
गदाधरं विबुधजनैरभिष्टुतं
धृतक्षमं क्षुधितजनार्त्तिनाशनम् ।
शिवं विशालासुरसैन्यमर्दनं
नमाम्यहं हतसकलाशुभं स्मृतौ ॥ 7.29 ॥
7.m:
Raibhya said:
'I bow to Gadādhara, praised by the wise, / who bears forbearance, who destroys the affliction of hungry people, / auspicious, the crusher of the vast demon army, / who removes all misfortune when remembered;

7.s:
purāṇapūrvaṃ puruṣaṃ puruṣṭṛtaṃ
purātanaṃ vimalamalaṃ nṛṇāṃ gatim .
trivikramaṃ dhṛtadharaṇiṃ balerhaṃ
gadādharaṃ rahasi namāmi keśavam .. 7.30 ..
7.d:
पुराणपूर्वं पुरुषं पुरुष्टृतं
पुरातनं विमलमलं नृणां गतिम् ।
त्रिविक्रमं धृतधरणिं बलेर्हं
गदाधरं रहसि नमामि केशवम् ॥ 7.30 ॥
7.m: the primal person prior to the ancient, widely praised, / the eternal, pure, who is the refuge of men, / Trivikrama, who holds the Earth, who subdued Bali, / Gadādhara, Keśava, I bow to him in secret;

7.s:
suśuddhabhāvaṃ vibhavairupāvṛtaṃ
śriyāvṛtaṃ vigatamalaṃ vicakṣaṇam .
kṣitīśvarairapagatakilbiṣaiḥ stutaṃ
gadādharaṃ praṇamati yaḥ sukhaṃ vaset .. 7.31 ..
7.d:
सुशुद्धभावं विभवैरुपावृतं
श्रियावृतं विगतमलं विचक्षणम् ।
क्षितीश्वरैरपगतकिल्बिषैः स्तुतं
गदाधरं प्रणमति यः सुखं वसेत् ॥ 7.31 ॥
7.m: whose nature is purely stainless, surrounded by glories, / enveloped by Śrī, free from taint, discerning; / he who bows to Gadādhara, praised by kings whose sins are dispelled, / shall dwell in happiness.'

7.s:
surāsurairarccitapādapaṅkajaṃ
keyūrahārāṅgadamaulidhāriṇam .
abdhau śayānaṃ ca rathāṅgapāṇinaṃ
gadādharaṃ praṇamati yaḥ sukhaṃ vaset .. 7.32 ..
7.d:
सुरासुरैरर्च्चितपादपङ्कजं
केयूरहाराङ्गदमौलिधारिणम् ।
अब्धौ शयानं च रथाङ्गपाणिनं
गदाधरं प्रणमति यः सुखं वसेत् ॥ 7.32 ॥
7.m: Whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods and asuras, / who wears armlets, necklaces, bracelets, and a crown, / who sleeps upon the ocean and holds a discus in his hand— / whoever bows to Gadādhara shall dwell in happiness.

7.s:
sitaṃ kṛte tretāyuge'ruṇaṃ vibhuṃ
tathā tṛtīye pītavarṇamacyutam .
kalau ghanālipratimaṃ maheśvaraṃ
gadādharaṃ praṇamati yaḥ sukhaṃ vaset .. 7.33 ..
7.d:
सितं कृते त्रेतायुगेऽरुणं विभुं
तथा तृतीये पीतवर्णमच्युतम् ।
कलौ घनालिप्रतिमं महेश्वरं
गदाधरं प्रणमति यः सुखं वसेत् ॥ 7.33 ॥
7.m: White in the Kṛta yuga, reddish in the Tretā yuga, the all-pervading Lord, / likewise yellow-coloured in the third, the infallible one, / like a dense row of clouds in the Kali yuga, the great Lord— / whoever bows to Gadādhara shall dwell in happiness.

7.s:
bījodbhavo yaḥ sṛjate caturmukha-
stathaiva nārāyaṇarūpato jagat .
prapālayed rudravapustathāntakṛd
gadādharo jayatu ṣaḍarddhamūrtimān .. 7.34 ..
7.d:
बीजोद्भवो यः सृजते चतुर्मुख-
स्तथैव नारायणरूपतो जगत् ।
प्रपालयेद् रुद्रवपुस्तथान्तकृद्
गदाधरो जयतु षडर्द्धमूर्तिमान् ॥ 7.34 ॥
7.m: He who, arisen from the seed, as four-faced [Brahmā] creates, / and likewise in the form of Nārāyaṇa protects the universe, / and in the form of Rudra brings an end to it— / may Gadādhara, having the triple form, be victorious.

7.s:
sattvaṃ rajaścaiva tamo guṇāstraya-
stveteṣu nānyasya samudbhavaḥ kila .
sa caika eva trividho gadādharo
dadhātu dhairyaṃ mama dharmamokṣayoḥ .. 7.35 ..
7.d:
सत्त्वं रजश्चैव तमो गुणास्त्रय-
स्त्वेतेषु नान्यस्य समुद्भवः किल ।
स चैक एव त्रिविधो गदाधरो
दधातु धैर्यं मम धर्ममोक्षयोः ॥ 7.35 ॥
7.m: Sattva, rajas, and tamas are the three guṇas; / indeed, nothing else has come into being through these. / He is the one single Gadādhara in threefold aspect; / may he grant me steadfastness in righteousness and liberation.

7.s:
saṃsāratoyārṇavaduḥkhatantubhi-
rviyoganakrakramaṇaiḥ subhīṣaṇaiḥ .
majjantamuccaiḥ sutarāṃ mahāplave
gadādharo māmu dadhātu potavat .. 7.36 ..
7.d:
संसारतोयार्णवदुःखतन्तुभि-
र्वियोगनक्रक्रमणैः सुभीषणैः ।
मज्जन्तमुच्चैः सुतरां महाप्लवे
गदाधरो मामु दधातु पोतवत् ॥ 7.36 ॥
7.m: In this ocean of the water of saṃsāra, by the threads of sorrow, / by the exceedingly terrifying attacks of the crocodiles of separation, / as I sink deeply, may Gadādhara lift me up / like a boat onto the great raft.

7.s:
svayaṃ trimūrtiḥ svamivātmanātmani
svaśaktitaścāṇḍamidaṃ sasarjja ha .
tasmiñjalotthāsanamāryatejasaṃ
sasarjja yastaṃ praṇato'smi bhūdharam .. 7.37 ..
7.d:
स्वयं त्रिमूर्तिः स्वमिवात्मनात्मनि
स्वशक्तितश्चाण्डमिदं ससर्ज्ज ह ।
तस्मिञ्जलोत्थासनमार्यतेजसं
ससर्ज्ज यस्तं प्रणतोऽस्मि भूधरम् ॥ 7.37 ॥
7.m: Himself of triple form, he created this cosmic egg from himself / through his own power, as if from his own self within himself. / I bow to that supporter of the earth who created / [Brahmā] of noble splendour, seated upon what rose from the water.

7.s:
matsyādināmāni jagatsu kevalaṃ
surādisaṃrakṣaṇato vṛṣākapiḥ .
mukhyasvarūpeṇa samantato vibhu-
rgadādharo me vidadhātu sadgatim .. 7.38 ..
7.d:
मत्स्यादिनामानि जगत्सु केवलं
सुरादिसंरक्षणतो वृषाकपिः ।
मुख्यस्वरूपेण समन्ततो विभु-
र्गदाधरो मे विदधातु सद्गतिम् ॥ 7.38 ॥
7.m: Taking names such as Matsya merely in the worlds / for the protection of gods and others, Vṛṣākapi, / the all-pervading Gadādhara in his primary form in every direction— / may he grant me the supreme destination.

7.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
evaṃ stutastadā viṣṇurbhaktyā raibhyeṇa dhīmatā .
prādurbabhūva sahasā pītavāsā janārdanaḥ .. 7.39 ..
7.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
एवं स्तुतस्तदा विष्णुर्भक्त्या रैभ्येण धीमता ।
प्रादुर्बभूव सहसा पीतवासा जनार्दनः ॥ 7.39 ॥
7.m: Śrī Varāha said: / Thus praised then with devotion by the wise Raibhya, / Viṣṇu Janārdana, clad in yellow garments, suddenly appeared.

7.s:
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇirgaruḍastho viyadgataḥ .
uvāca meghagambhīradhīravāk puruṣottamaḥ .. 7.40 ..
7.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिर्गरुडस्थो वियद्गतः ।
उवाच मेघगम्भीरधीरवाक् पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ 7.40 ॥
7.m: Holding conch, discus, and mace, seated on Garuḍa, moving in the sky, / the Supreme Person spoke with a voice deep and grave as a cloud:

7.s:
tuṣṭo'smi raibhya bhaktyā te stutyā ca dvijasattama .
tīrthasnānena ca vibho brūhi yatte'bhivāñchitam .. 7.41 ..
7.d:
तुष्टोऽस्मि रैभ्य भक्त्या ते स्तुत्या च द्विजसत्तम ।
तीर्थस्नानेन च विभो ब्रूहि यत्तेऽभिवाञ्छितम् ॥ 7.41 ॥
7.m: “I am pleased, O Raibhya, best of the twice-born, with your devotion, / with your hymn of praise, and with your bathing at the tīrtha. Speak, O mighty one, of what you desire.”

7.s:
raibhya uvāca .
gatiṃ me dehi deveśa yatra te sanakādayaḥ .
vaseyaṃ tatra yenāhaṃ tvatprasādād gadādhara .. 7.42 ..
7.d:
रैभ्य उवाच ।
गतिं मे देहि देवेश यत्र ते सनकादयः ।
वसेयं तत्र येनाहं त्वत्प्रसादाद् गदाधर ॥ 7.42 ॥
7.m: Raibhya said: / “Grant me that state, O Lord of gods, where Sanaka and the others dwell, / so that by your grace I may dwell there, O Gadādhara.”

7.s:
deva uvāca .
evamastviti te brahmannityuktvā'ntaradhīyata .
bhagavānapi raibhyastu divyajñānasamanvitaḥ .. 7.43 ..
7.d:
देव उवाच ।
एवमस्त्विति ते ब्रह्मन्नित्युक्त्वाऽन्तरधीयत ।
भगवानपि रैभ्यस्तु दिव्यज्ञानसमन्वितः ॥ 7.43 ॥
7.m: The god said: / “May it be so for you, O Brahmin!” Having said this, he vanished. / And Raibhya, endowed with divine knowledge by the Lord,

7.s:
kṣaṇād babhūva devena parituṣṭena cakriṇā .
jagāma yatra te siddhāḥ sanakādyā maharṣayaḥ .. 7.44 ..
7.d:
क्षणाद् बभूव देवेन परितुष्टेन चक्रिणा ।
जगाम यत्र ते सिद्धाः सनकाद्या महर्षयः ॥ 7.44 ॥
7.m: instantly became [so transformed] by the god, the wielder of the discus, who was well pleased. / He went to the place where those perfected ones, Sanaka and the other great seers, dwell.

7.s:
etacca raibhyanirddiṣṭaṃ stotraṃ viṣṇorgadābhṛtaḥ .
yaḥ paṭhet sa gayāṃ gatvā piṇḍadānād viśiṣyate .. 7.45 ..
7.d:
एतच्च रैभ्यनिर्द्दिष्टं स्तोत्रं विष्णोर्गदाभृतः ।
यः पठेत् स गयां गत्वा पिण्डदानाद् विशिष्यते ॥ 7.45 ॥
7.m: And whoever recites this hymn to Viṣṇu Gadābhṛt, taught by Raibhya, / attains more than by going to Gayā and offering a rice-ball.

7.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre saptamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 7 ..
7.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे सप्तमोऽध्यायः ॥ 7 ॥
7.m: Thus ends the seventh chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, a scripture of the Lord.

8.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
yo'sau vasoḥ śarīre tuvyādho bhūtvā nṛpasya ha .
sa svavṛttyāṃ sthitaḥ kālaṃ caturvarṣasahastrikam .. 8.1 ..
8.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
योऽसौ वसोः शरीरे तुव्याधो भूत्वा नृपस्य ह ।
स स्ववृत्त्यां स्थितः कालं चतुर्वर्षसहस्त्रिकम् ॥ 8.1 ॥
8.m: Śrī Varāha said: / He who, in the body of King Vasu, became a hunter, / remained established in his own occupation for a period of four thousand years.

8.s:
ekaikaṃ svakuṭumbārthe hatvā vanacaraṃ mṛgam .
bhṛtyātithihutāśānāṃ prīṇanaṃ kurute sadā .. 8.2 ..
8.d:
एकैकं स्वकुटुम्बार्थे हत्वा वनचरं मृगम् ।
भृत्यातिथिहुताशानां प्रीणनं कुरुते सदा ॥ 8.2 ॥
8.m: Killing one forest-dwelling deer each day for the sake of his family, / he constantly satisfied his servants, guests, and the sacred fire.

8.s:
mithilāyāṃ varārohe sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi .
pitṝṇāṃ kurute śrāddhaṃ svācāreṇa vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 8.3 ..
8.d:
मिथिलायां वरारोहे सदा पर्वणि पर्वणि ।
पितॄणां कुरुते श्राद्धं स्वाचारेण विचक्षणः ॥ 8.3 ॥
8.m: In Mithilā, O fair-hipped one, always on the sacred festival days, / the wise man performed the ancestral offering to the ancestors according to his own custom.

8.s:
agniṃ paricaran nityaṃ vadan satyaṃ subhāṣitam .
prāṇayātrānusaktastu yo'sau jīvaṃ na pātayet .. 8.4 ..
8.d:
अग्निं परिचरन् नित्यं वदन् सत्यं सुभाषितम् ।
प्राणयात्रानुसक्तस्तु योऽसौ जीवं न पातयेत् ॥ 8.4 ॥
8.m: Constantly tending the sacred fire, speaking the truth that was well uttered, / intent only upon maintaining life, he did not destroy living beings [unnecessarily].

8.s:
evaṃ tu vasatastasya dharmabuddhirmahātapāḥ .
putrastvarjunako nāma babhūva munivadvaśī .. 8.5 ..
8.d:
एवं तु वसतस्तस्य धर्मबुद्धिर्महातपाः ।
पुत्रस्त्वर्जुनको नाम बभूव मुनिवद्वशी ॥ 8.5 ॥
8.m: As he lived thus, righteous in mind and of great asceticism, / a son named Arjunaka was born to him, self-controlled like a sage.

8.s:
tasya kālena mahatā cāritreṇa ca dhīmataḥ .
babhūvārjjunakī nāma kanyā ca varavarṇinī .. 8.6 ..
8.d:
तस्य कालेन महता चारित्रेण च धीमतः ।
बभूवार्ज्जुनकी नाम कन्या च वरवर्णिनी ॥ 8.6 ॥
8.m: In the course of much time, by the conduct of that wise man, / a daughter named Arjunakī was born, a woman of excellent complexion.

8.s:
tasyā yauvanakāle tu cintayāmāsa dharmavit .
kasyeyaṃ dīyate kanyā ko vā yogyaśca vai pumān .. 8.7 ..
8.d:
तस्या यौवनकाले तु चिन्तयामास धर्मवित् ।
कस्येयं दीयते कन्या को वा योग्यश्च वै पुमान् ॥ 8.7 ॥
8.m: When the time of her youth arrived, the knower of righteousness reflected: / “To whom should this maiden be given? What man is suitable?”

8.s:
iti cintayatastasya mataṅgasya sutaṃ prati .
dharmavyādhasya suvyaktaṃ prasannākhyaṃ prati bruvan .. 8.8 ..
8.d:
इति चिन्तयतस्तस्य मतङ्गस्य सुतं प्रति ।
धर्मव्याधस्य सुव्यक्तं प्रसन्नाख्यं प्रति ब्रुवन् ॥ 8.8 ॥
8.m: As he was thus reflecting with regard to the son of Mataṅga, / clearly speaking to the one named Prasanna on behalf of the righteous hunter,

8.s:
evaṃ saṃcintya mātaṅgaḥ prasannaṃ prati sodyataḥ .
uvāca tasya pitaraṃ prasannāyārjjunīṃ bhavān .
gṛhāṇa tapatāṃ śreṣṭha svayaṃ dattāṃ mahātmane .. 8.9 ..
8.d:
एवं संचिन्त्य मातङ्गः प्रसन्नं प्रति सोद्यतः ।
उवाच तस्य पितरं प्रसन्नायार्ज्जुनीं भवान् ।
गृहाण तपतां श्रेष्ठ स्वयं दत्तां महात्मने ॥ 8.9 ॥
8.m: having thus reflected, he set out toward Prasanna, the son of Mataṅga, / and said to his father: “Accept Arjunī for Prasanna, / O best of ascetics, given by me of my own accord to the great-souled one.”

8.s:
mataṅga uvāca .
prasanno'yaṃ mama sutaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ .
gṛhṇāmyarjunakīṃ kanyāṃ tvatsutāṃ vyādhasattama .. 8.10 ..
8.d:
मतङ्ग उवाच ।
प्रसन्नोऽयं मम सुतः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ।
गृह्णाम्यर्जुनकीं कन्यां त्वत्सुतां व्याधसत्तम ॥ 8.10 ॥
8.m: Mataṅga said: / “This son of mine, Prasanna, is skilled in all sacred scriptures. / I accept the maiden Arjunakī, your daughter, O best of hunters.”

8.s:
evamukte tadā kanyāṃ dharmavyādho mahātapāḥ .
mataṅgaputrāya dadau prasannāya ca dhīmate .. 8.11 ..
8.d:
एवमुक्ते तदा कन्यां धर्मव्याधो महातपाः ।
मतङ्गपुत्राय ददौ प्रसन्नाय च धीमते ॥ 8.11 ॥
8.m: When this was said, the righteous hunter of great asceticism / gave the maiden to Mataṅga's son, the wise Prasanna.

8.s:
dharmavyādhastadā kanyāṃ datvā svagṛhamīyivān .
sā'pi śvaśurayorbhartuḥ śuśrīṣaṇaparā'bhavat .. 8.12 ..
8.d:
धर्मव्याधस्तदा कन्यां दत्वा स्वगृहमीयिवान् ।
साऽपि श्वशुरयोर्भर्तुः शुश्रीषणपराऽभवत् ॥ 8.12 ॥
8.m: Then, having given the maiden away, the righteous hunter went to his home. / And she was devoted to serving her parents-in-law and her husband.

8.s:
atha kālena mahatā sā kanyā'rjunakī śubhā .
uktā śvaśruvā sutā putri jīvahantustvamīdṛśī .
na jānāsi tapaścartuṃ bhartturārādhanaṃ tathā .. 8.13 ..
8.d:
अथ कालेन महता सा कन्याऽर्जुनकी शुभा ।
उक्ता श्वश्रुवा सुता पुत्रि जीवहन्तुस्त्वमीदृशी ।
न जानासि तपश्चर्तुं भर्त्तुराराधनं तथा ॥ 8.13 ॥
8.m: Then, after a long time, that auspicious maiden Arjunakī / was told by her mother-in-law: “Daughter, you are the child of a killer of living creatures! / Being such, you do not know how to practice asceticism or to worship your husband.”

8.s:
sā'pi svalpāparādhena bhartsitā tanumadhyamā .
piturveśmagatā bālā rodamānā muhurmuhuḥ .. 8.14 ..
8.d:
साऽपि स्वल्पापराधेन भर्त्सिता तनुमध्यमा ।
पितुर्वेश्मगता बाला रोदमाना मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 8.14 ॥
8.m: Reproached thus for a small fault, the slender-waisted young woman / went to her father's house, weeping again and again.

8.s:
pitrā pṛṣṭā kimetat te putri rodanakāraṇam .
evamuktā tadā sā tu kathayāmāsa bhāminī .. 8.15 ..
8.d:
पित्रा पृष्टा किमेतत् ते पुत्रि रोदनकारणम् ।
एवमुक्ता तदा सा तु कथयामास भामिनी ॥ 8.15 ॥
8.m: Asked by her father: “What is this, my daughter? What is the cause of your weeping?” / Being thus addressed, that lovely woman recounted:

8.s:
śvaśvrā'hamuktā tīvreṇa kopena mahatā pitaḥ .
jīvahantuḥ sutetyuccairasakṛd vyādhajeti ca .. 8.16 ..
8.d:
श्वश्व्राऽहमुक्ता तीव्रेण कोपेन महता पितः ।
जीवहन्तुः सुतेत्युच्चैरसकृद् व्याधजेति च ॥ 8.16 ॥
8.m: “I was addressed by my mother-in-law with sharp and great anger, O father: / ‘Daughter of a killer of living beings!’ and ‘Born of a hunter!’ loudly, repeatedly.”

8.s:
etacchrutvā sa dharmātmā dharmavyādho ruṣānvitaḥ .
mataṅgasya gṛhaṃ so'tha gatvā janapadairvṛtam .. 8.17 ..
8.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा स धर्मात्मा धर्मव्याधो रुषान्वितः ।
मतङ्गस्य गृहं सोऽथ गत्वा जनपदैर्वृतम् ॥ 8.17 ॥
8.m: Having heard this, the righteous-souled hunter, filled with anger, / went to Mataṅga's house, which was surrounded by country folk.

8.s:
tasyāgatasya saṃbandhī mataṅgo jayatāṃ varaḥ .
āsanādyardhyapādyena pūjayitvedamabravīt .
kimāgamanakṛtyaṃ te kiṃ karomyāgatakriyām .. 8.18 ..
8.d:
तस्यागतस्य संबन्धी मतङ्गो जयतां वरः ।
आसनाद्यर्ध्यपाद्येन पूजयित्वेदमब्रवीत् ।
किमागमनकृत्यं ते किं करोम्यागतक्रियाम् ॥ 8.18 ॥
8.m: When he had arrived, his relative by marriage, Mataṅga, best of victorious men, / honoured him with a seat, guest-water, and foot-water, and said this: / ‘What is the purpose of your arrival? What hospitality may I perform for you who have come?’

8.s:
vyādha uvāca .
bhojanaṃ kiṃcidicchāmi bhoktuṃ caitanyavarjitam .
kautūhalena yenāhamāgato bhavato gṛham .. 8.19 ..
8.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
भोजनं किंचिदिच्छामि भोक्तुं चैतन्यवर्जितम् ।
कौतूहलेन येनाहमागतो भवतो गृहम् ॥ 8.19 ॥
8.m: The hunter said: / ‘I wish to eat some food that is devoid of consciousness; / out of curiosity for that, I have come to your house.’

8.s:
mataṅga uvāca .
godhūmā vrīmayaścaiva saṃskṛtā mama veśmani .
bhujyatāṃ dharmavicchreṣṭha yathākāmaṃ tapodhana .. 8.20 ..
8.d:
मतङ्ग उवाच ।
गोधूमा व्रीमयश्चैव संस्कृता मम वेश्मनि ।
भुज्यतां धर्मविच्छ्रेष्ठ यथाकामं तपोधन ॥ 8.20 ॥
8.m: Mataṅga said: / ‘Wheat and rice are prepared in my house. / Eat, O best among the knowers of righteousness, as you desire, O rich in asceticism.’

8.s:
vyādha uvāca .
paśyāmi kīdṛśāste hi godhūmā vrīhayo yavāḥ .
svarūpeṇa ca santyete yena vo vedmi sattama .. 8.21 ..
8.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
पश्यामि कीदृशास्ते हि गोधूमा व्रीहयो यवाः ।
स्वरूपेण च सन्त्येते येन वो वेद्मि सत्तम ॥ 8.21 ॥
8.m: The hunter said: / ‘Let me see what your wheat, rice, and barley are like, / and in what natural form they exist, so that I may understand you, O best of men.’

8.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
evamukte mataṅgena śūrpaṃ godhūmapūritam .
aparaṃ tatra vrīhīṇāṃ dharmavyādhāya darśitam .. 8.22 ..
8.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
एवमुक्ते मतङ्गेन शूर्पं गोधूमपूरितम् ।
अपरं तत्र व्रीहीणां धर्मव्याधाय दर्शितम् ॥ 8.22 ॥
8.m: Śrī Varāha said: / When this was said, a winnowing basket filled with wheat / and another with rice were shown by Mataṅga to the righteous hunter.

8.s:
dṛṣṭvā vrīhīn sagodhūmān dharmavyādho varāsanāt .
utthāya gantumārebhe mataṅgena nivāritaḥ .. 8.23 ..
8.d:
दृष्ट्वा व्रीहीन् सगोधूमान् धर्मव्याधो वरासनात् ।
उत्थाय गन्तुमारेभे मतङ्गेन निवारितः ॥ 8.23 ॥
8.m: Having seen the rice along with the wheat, the righteous hunter / stood up from his noble seat and began to leave, but was prevented by Mataṅga.

8.s:
kimarthaṃ gantumārabdhaṃ tvayā vada mahāmate .
abhuktenaiva saṃsiddhaṃ madgṛhe cānnamuttamam .
pācayitvā svayaṃ caiva kasmāt tvaṃ nādya bhuñjase .. 8.24 ..
8.d:
किमर्थं गन्तुमारब्धं त्वया वद महामते ।
अभुक्तेनैव संसिद्धं मद्गृहे चान्नमुत्तमम् ।
पाचयित्वा स्वयं चैव कस्मात् त्वं नाद्य भुञ्जसे ॥ 8.24 ॥
8.m: "Speak, O noble-minded one! Why have you started to leave / without eating, when excellent food is prepared in my house? / Having cooked it yourself, why do you not eat today?"

8.s:
vyādha uvāca .
sahastraśaḥ koṭiśaśca jīvān haṃsi dine dine .
athedṛśasya pāpasya ko'nnaṃ bhuñjati satpumān .. 8.25 ..
8.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
सहस्त्रशः कोटिशश्च जीवान् हंसि दिने दिने ।
अथेदृशस्य पापस्य कोऽन्नं भुञ्जति सत्पुमान् ॥ 8.25 ॥
8.m: The hunter said: / "Day after day you kill living beings by the thousands and tens of millions. / Who that is a good man eats the food of such a sinner?

8.s:
acaitanyaṃ yadi gṛhe vidyate'nnaṃ susaṃskṛtam .
idānīmatra saṃdṛṣṭā ete tu jalajantavaḥ .. 8.26 ..
8.d:
अचैतन्यं यदि गृहे विद्यतेऽन्नं सुसंस्कृतम् ।
इदानीमत्र संदृष्टा एते तु जलजन्तवः ॥ 8.26 ॥
8.m: If inanimate, well-prepared food is present in the house— / but just now these water-insects have been seen here.

8.s: (uptāḥ sahastratāṃ yānti pratisaṃvatsaraṃ mune .) .. 8.26 (1)..
8.d: (उप्ताः सहस्त्रतां यान्ति प्रतिसंवत्सरं मुने ।) ॥ 8.26 (1)॥

8.s:
ahamekaṃ kuṭumbārthe hanmyaraṇye paśuṃ dine .
taṃ cet pitṛbhyaḥ saṃskṛtya dattvā bhuñjāmi sānugaḥ .. 8.27 ..
8.d:
अहमेकं कुटुम्बार्थे हन्म्यरण्ये पशुं दिने ।
तं चेत् पितृभ्यः संस्कृत्य दत्त्वा भुञ्जामि सानुगः ॥ 8.27 ॥

8.s:
tvaṃ tu jīvān bahūn hatvā svakuṭumbena sānugaḥ .
bhuñjannetena satatamabhojyaṃ tanmataṃ mama .. 8.28 ..
8.d:
त्वं तु जीवान् बहून् हत्वा स्वकुटुम्बेन सानुगः ।
भुञ्जन्नेतेन सततमभोज्यं तन्मतं मम ॥ 8.28 ॥
8.m: You, however, having killed many living beings, / eat constantly along with your family and dependents; therefore it is inedible in my view.

8.s:
brahmaṇā tu purā sṛṣṭā oṣadhyaḥ sarvavīrudhaḥ .
yajñārthaṃ tattu bhūtānāṃ bhakṣyamityeva vai śrutiḥ .. 8.29 ..
8.d:
ब्रह्मणा तु पुरा सृष्टा ओषध्यः सर्ववीरुधः ।
यज्ञार्थं तत्तु भूतानां भक्ष्यमित्येव वै श्रुतिः ॥ 8.29 ॥
8.m: Herbs and all plants were created of old by Brahmā / for the purpose of sacrifice, and that is indeed food for living beings—so says the scripture.

8.s:
divyo bhautastathā paitro mānuṣo brāhma eva ca .
ete pañca mahāyajñā brahmaṇā nirmitāḥ purā .. 8.30 ..
8.d:
दिव्यो भौतस्तथा पैत्रो मानुषो ब्राह्म एव च ।
एते पञ्च महायज्ञा ब्रह्मणा निर्मिताः पुरा ॥ 8.30 ॥
8.m: The sacrifice to gods, that to spirits, that to ancestors, that to humans, and that to Brahman: / these five great sacrifices were fashioned of old by Brahmā

8.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ hitārthāya itareṣāṃ ca tanmukham .
itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ kāritāḥ śubhāḥ .. 8.31 ..
8.d:
ब्राह्मणानां हितार्थाय इतरेषां च तन्मुखम् ।
इतरेषां तु वर्णानां ब्राह्मणैः कारिताः शुभाः ॥ 8.31 ॥
8.m: for the welfare of Brahmins, and their mouth is the same for the others. / For the other castes, auspicious [rites] are caused to be performed by Brahmins.

8.s:
evaṃ yadi vibhāgaḥ syād varānnaṃ tad viśudhyati .
anyathā vrīhayo'pyete ekaike mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ .
mantavyā dātṛbhoktṛṇāṃ mahāmāṃsaṃ tu tat smṛtam .. 8.32 ..
8.d:
एवं यदि विभागः स्याद् वरान्नं तद् विशुध्यति ।
अन्यथा व्रीहयोऽप्येते एकैके मृगपक्षिणः ।
मन्तव्या दातृभोक्तृणां महामांसं तु तत् स्मृतम् ॥ 8.32 ॥
8.m: If such an allotment is observed, that excellent food is purified; / otherwise, even these grains of rice are each to be regarded / as beasts and birds for both the givers and the eaters, and that is considered 'great flesh'.

8.s:
mayā te duhitā dattā putrārthe devarūpiṇī .
sā ca tvadbhāryayā proktā duhitā jantughātinaḥ .. 8.33 ..
8.d:
मया ते दुहिता दत्ता पुत्रार्थे देवरूपिणी ।
सा च त्वद्भार्यया प्रोक्ता दुहिता जन्तुघातिनः ॥ 8.33 ॥
8.m: I gave you my daughter of godly form for your son, / and she was spoken of by your wife as 'the daughter of a killer of creatures'.

8.s:
ato'rthamāgato'haṃ te gṛhaṃ prati samīkṣitum .
ācāraṃ devapūjāṃ ca atithīnāṃ ca tarpaṇam .. 8.34 ..
8.d:
अतोऽर्थमागतोऽहं ते गृहं प्रति समीक्षितुम् ।
आचारं देवपूजां च अतिथीनां च तर्पणम् ॥ 8.34 ॥
8.m: For this reason I came to your house to observe / conduct, worship of the gods, and propitiation of guests.

8.s:
eteṣāmekamapyatra kurvannapi na dṛśyate .
tad gṛhaṃ gantumicchāmi pitṝṇāṃ śrāddhakāmyayā .. 8.35 ..
8.d:
एतेषामेकमप्यत्र कुर्वन्नपि न दृश्यते ।
तद् गृहं गन्तुमिच्छामि पितॄणां श्राद्धकाम्यया ॥ 8.35 ॥
8.m: Not one of these is seen being performed here. / Therefore I wish to go home, desiring to perform the ancestral rite for the ancestors.

8.s:
svagṛhe naiva bhuñjāmi pitṝṇāṃ kāryamityuta .
ahaṃ vyādho jīvaghātī na tu tvaṃ lokahiṃsakaḥ .. 8.36 ..
8.d:
स्वगृहे नैव भुञ्जामि पितॄणां कार्यमित्युत ।
अहं व्याधो जीवघाती न तु त्वं लोकहिंसकः ॥ 8.36 ॥
8.m: I do not eat in my own house when it is the work of the ancestors. / I am a hunter, a killer of creatures, but not a destroyer of the world as you are.

8.s:
matsutā jīvaghātasya yadoḍhā tvatsutena ca .
tanmahattvaṃ ca saṃjātaṃ prāyaścitaṃ tapodhana .. 8.37 ..
8.d:
मत्सुता जीवघातस्य यदोढा त्वत्सुतेन च ।
तन्महत्त्वं च संजातं प्रायश्चितं तपोधन ॥ 8.37 ॥
8.m: Since my daughter, born of a killer of creatures, was married by your son, / an atonement for that greatness has arisen, O rich in asceticism!"

8.s:
evamuktvā sa cotthāya śaptvā nārīṃ tadā dhare .
mā snuṣābhiḥ samaṃ śvaśrvā viśvāso bhavatu kvacit .. 8.38 ..
8.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स चोत्थाय शप्त्वा नारीं तदा धरे ।
मा स्नुषाभिः समं श्वश्र्वा विश्वासो भवतु क्वचित् ॥ 8.38 ॥
8.m: Having spoken thus, he rose up, and cursing the woman then, O Earth: / "Let there never be trust between daughters-in-law and a mother-in-law!

8.s:
mā ca snuṣā kadācit syād yā śvaśrūṃ jīvatīmiṣet .
evamuktvā gato vyādhaḥ svagṛhaṃ prati bhāmini .. 8.39 ..
8.d:
मा च स्नुषा कदाचित् स्याद् या श्वश्रूं जीवतीमिषेत् ।
एवमुक्त्वा गतो व्याधः स्वगृहं प्रति भामिनि ॥ 8.39 ॥
8.m: And let there never be a daughter-in-law who wishes her mother-in-law to live!" / Having spoken thus, the hunter went to his own home, O beautiful woman.

8.s:
tato devān pitṝn bhaktayā pūjayitvā vicakṣaṇaḥ .
putraṃ cārjunakaṃ sthāpya svasantāne mahātapāḥ .. 8.40 ..
8.d:
ततो देवान् पितॄन् भक्तया पूजयित्वा विचक्षणः ।
पुत्रं चार्जुनकं स्थाप्य स्वसन्ताने महातपाः ॥ 8.40 ॥
8.m: Then the wise one, having worshiped the gods and the ancestors with devotion, / and having established his son Arjanaka in his lineage, the one of great asceticism,

8.s:
dharmavyādho jagāmāśu tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam .
puruṣottamākhyaṃ ca paraṃ tatra gatvā samāhitaḥ .
tapaścacāra niyataḥ paṭhan stotramidaṃ dhare .. 8.41 ..
8.d:
धर्मव्याधो जगामाशु तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ।
पुरुषोत्तमाख्यं च परं तत्र गत्वा समाहितः ।
तपश्चचार नियतः पठन् स्तोत्रमिदं धरे ॥ 8.41 ॥
8.m: Dharmavyādha quickly went to the sacred bathing site renowned in the three worlds, / named Puruṣottama, the supreme; having gone there, concentrated in mind, / restrained, he practiced austerity, reciting this hymn of praise, O Earth:

8.s:
namāmi viṣṇuṃ tridaśārināśanaṃ
viśālavakṣasthalasaṃśritaśriyam .
suśāsanaṃ nītimatāṃ parāṃ gatiṃ
trivikramaṃ mandaradhāriṇaṃ sadā .. 8.42 ..
8.d:
नमामि विष्णुं त्रिदशारिनाशनं
विशालवक्षस्थलसंश्रितश्रियम् ।
सुशासनं नीतिमतां परां गतिं
त्रिविक्रमं मन्दरधारिणं सदा ॥ 8.42 ॥
8.m: "I bow to Viṣṇu, destroyer of the enemies of the thirty [gods], / whose broad chest is the resort of Śrī, / the good ruler, the supreme goal of the righteous, / Trivikrama, who ever supports Mount Mandara;

8.s:
dāmodaraṃ rañjitabhūtalaṃ dhiyā
yaśoṃśuśubhraṃ bhramarāṅgasaprabham .
dharādharaṃ narakaripuṃ puruṣṭutaṃ
namāmi viṣṇuṃ śaraṇaṃ janārdanam .. 8.43 ..
8.d:
दामोदरं रञ्जितभूतलं धिया
यशोंशुशुभ्रं भ्रमराङ्गसप्रभम् ।
धराधरं नरकरिपुं पुरुष्टुतं
नमामि विष्णुं शरणं जनार्दनम् ॥ 8.43 ॥
8.m: Dāmodara, who delights the surface of the earth through intellect, / white with the rays of fame, possessed of the luster of a bee's body, / the bearer of the earth, the foe of Naraka, praised by many: / I bow to Viṣṇu Janārdana as refuge.

8.s:
(naraṃ nṛsiṃhaṃ harimīśvaraṃ prabhuṃ
tridhāmanāmānamanantavarcasam .
susaṃskṛtāsyaṃ śaraṇaṃ narottamaṃ
vrajāmi devaṃ satataṃ tamacyutam .. 8.43 (1))
tridhā sthitaṃ tigmarathāṅgapāṇinaṃ
nayasthitaṃ tṛptamanuttamairguṇaiḥ .
niḥśreyasākhyaṃ kṣapitetaraṃ guruṃ
namāmi viṣṇuṃ puruṣottamaṃ tvaham .. 8.44 ..
8.d:
(नरं नृसिंहं हरिमीश्वरं प्रभुं
त्रिधामनामानमनन्तवर्चसम् ।
सुसंस्कृतास्यं शरणं नरोत्तमं
व्रजामि देवं सततं तमच्युतम् ॥ 8.43 (1))
त्रिधा स्थितं तिग्मरथाङ्गपाणिनं
नयस्थितं तृप्तमनुत्तमैर्गुणैः ।
निःश्रेयसाख्यं क्षपितेतरं गुरुं
नमामि विष्णुं पुरुषोत्तमं त्वहम् ॥ 8.44 ॥
8.m: (I ever go for refuge to the god Acyuta, best among men, / Nara, Nṛsiṃha, Hari, the Lord, the master, / named of three abodes, of endless splendor, / whose mouth is well adorned.) / I bow indeed to Viṣṇu, Puruṣottama, / who abides threefold, holding the sharp discus in his hand, / abiding in righteousness, satisfied by unsurpassable virtues, / known as the highest good, who destroys all else, the Guru.

8.s:
(hatau purāṇau madhukaiṭabhāvubhau
bibhartti ca kṣmāṃ śirasā sadā hi saḥ .
yathā stuto me prasabhaṃ sanātano
dadhātu viṣṇuḥ sukhamūrjitaṃ mama .. 8.44 (1))
mahāvarāho haviṣāmbubhojano
janārdano me hitakṛccitīmukhaḥ .
kṣitīdharo māmudadhikṣayo mahān
sa pātu viṣṇuḥ śaraṇārthinaṃ tu mām .. 8.45 ..
8.d:
(हतौ पुराणौ मधुकैटभावुभौ
बिभर्त्ति च क्ष्मां शिरसा सदा हि सः ।
यथा स्तुतो मे प्रसभं सनातनो
दधातु विष्णुः सुखमूर्जितं मम ॥ 8.44 (1))
महावराहो हविषाम्बुभोजनो
जनार्दनो मे हितकृच्चितीमुखः ।
क्षितीधरो मामुदधिक्षयो महान्
स पातु विष्णुः शरणार्थिनं तु माम् ॥ 8.45 ॥
8.m: (The two ancient ones, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, were slain [by him], / and he indeed constantly supports the earth on his head. / As he is praised by me, may the eternal Viṣṇu / forcibly bestow immense happiness upon me.) / The great Varāha, whose food is sacrificial oblations and water, / Janārdana, who works my welfare, whose face is the funeral pyre, / the bearer of the earth, the great destroyer of the ocean— / may that Viṣṇu protect me who seek refuge!

8.s:
māyātataṃ yena jagattrayaṃ kṛtaṃ
yathāgninaikena tataṃ carācaram .
carācarasya svayameva sarvataḥ
sa me'stu viṣṇuḥ śaraṇaṃ jagatpatiḥ .. 8.46 ..
8.d:
मायाततं येन जगत्त्रयं कृतं
यथाग्निनैकेन ततं चराचरम् ।
चराचरस्य स्वयमेव सर्वतः
स मेऽस्तु विष्णुः शरणं जगत्पतिः ॥ 8.46 ॥
8.m: By whom the three worlds were made stretched out with creative illusion, / just as the moving and unmoving are pervaded by a single fire; / may that Viṣṇu, Lord of the world, / himself all around, be my refuge!

8.s:
bhave bhave yaśca sasarjja kaṃ tato
jagat prasūtaṃ sacarācaraṃ tvidam .
tataśca rudrātmavati pralīyate-
'nvato harirviṣṇuharastathocyate .. 8.47 ..
8.d:
भवे भवे यश्च ससर्ज्ज कं ततो
जगत् प्रसूतं सचराचरं त्विदम् ।
ततश्च रुद्रात्मवति प्रलीयते-
ऽन्वतो हरिर्विष्णुहरस्तथोच्यते ॥ 8.47 ॥
8.m: And who in birth after birth created Brahmā, from whom / this world of moving and unmoving was brought forth, / and then dissolves into the one who has the nature of Rudra— / therefore Hari is spoken of as both Viṣṇu and Hara.

8.s:
khātmendupṛthvīpavanāgnibhāskarā
jalaṃ ca yasya prabhavanti mūrttayaḥ .
sa sarvadā me bhagavān sanātano
dadātu śaṃ viṣṇuracintyarūpadhṛk .. 8.48 ..
8.d:
खात्मेन्दुपृथ्वीपवनाग्निभास्करा
जलं च यस्य प्रभवन्ति मूर्त्तयः ।
स सर्वदा मे भगवान् सनातनो
ददातु शं विष्णुरचिन्त्यरूपधृक् ॥ 8.48 ॥
8.m: Whose forms are space, self, moon, earth, wind, fire, sun, / and water: / may that eternal Lord Viṣṇu, / who bears an unthinkable form, always bestow welfare upon me!"

8.s:
itīrite tasya sanātanaḥ svayaṃ
puro babhūvādbhutarūpadarśanaḥ .
8.d:
इतीरिते तस्य सनातनः स्वयं
पुरो बभूवाद्भुतरूपदर्शनः ।
8.m: When this was spoken by him, the eternal one himself / appeared before him, marvelous in appearance to behold.

9.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
ādau kṛtayuge nātha kiṃ kṛtaṃ viśvamūrttinā .
nārāyaṇena tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ .. 9.1 ..
9.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
आदौ कृतयुगे नाथ किं कृतं विश्वमूर्त्तिना ।
नारायणेन तत्सर्वं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥ 9.1 ॥
9.m: Dharaṇī said: / "In the beginning, in the Kṛta yuga, O Lord, what was done by the universal-formed / Nārāyaṇa? I desire to hear all that in truth."

9.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
pūrvaṃ nārāyaṇastveko nāsīt kiñciddhareḥ param .
saika eva ratiṃ lebhe naiva svacchandakarmakṛt .. 9.2 ..
9.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
पूर्वं नारायणस्त्वेको नासीत् किञ्चिद्धरेः परम् ।
सैक एव रतिं लेभे नैव स्वच्छन्दकर्मकृत् ॥ 9.2 ॥
9.m: The holy Varāha said: / "Formerly, Nārāyaṇa alone existed; there was nothing beyond Hari. / He, being only one, found no delight, acting according to his own free will.

9.s:
tasya dvitīyamicchantaścintā buddhyātmikā babhau .
asāvityeva saṃjñāyā kṣaṇaṃ bhāskarasannibhā .. 9.3 ..
9.d:
तस्य द्वितीयमिच्छन्तश्चिन्ता बुद्ध्यात्मिका बभौ ।
असावित्येव संज्ञाया क्षणं भास्करसन्निभा ॥ 9.3 ॥
9.m: As he was desiring a second, a thought consisting of intellect shone forth, / named 'She', resembling the sun for a moment.

9.s:
tasyā api dvidhā bhūtā cintā'bhūda brahmavādinī .
umeti saṃjñayā yattatsadā martye vyavasthitā .. 9.4 ..
9.d:
तस्या अपि द्विधा भूता चिन्ताऽभूद ब्रह्मवादिनी ।
उमेति संज्ञया यत्तत्सदा मर्त्ये व्यवस्थिता ॥ 9.4 ॥
9.m: Of that [thought] also, a twofold thought declaring the absolute arose, / under the name Umā, which is ever stationed among mortals.

9.s:
omityekākṣarībhūtā sasarjemāṃ mahīṃ tadā .
bhūḥ sasarja bhuvaṃ so'pi svaḥ sasarja tato mahaḥ .. 9.5 ..
9.d:
ओमित्येकाक्षरीभूता ससर्जेमां महीं तदा ।
भूः ससर्ज भुवं सोऽपि स्वः ससर्ज ततो महः ॥ 9.5 ॥
9.m: Having become the single syllable 'oṃ', she then created this earth. / He created Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and then Svaḥ and Mahaḥ.

9.s:
tataśca jana ityeva tapaścātmā pralīyate .
etadotaṃ tathā protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva .. 9.6 ..
9.d:
ततश्च जन इत्येव तपश्चात्मा प्रलीयते ।
एतदोतं तथा प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥ 9.6 ॥
9.m: And then Janaḥ, Tapas, and the self is dissolved. / This is woven warp and woof, like rows of pearls upon a thread.

9.s:
jagat praṇavato bhūtaṃ śūnyametat sthitaṃ tadā .
yeyaṃ mūrtirbhagavataḥ śaṃkaraḥ sa svayaṃ hariḥ .. 9.7 ..
9.d:
जगत् प्रणवतो भूतं शून्यमेतत् स्थितं तदा ।
येयं मूर्तिर्भगवतः शंकरः स स्वयं हरिः ॥ 9.7 ॥
9.m: The world arose from the praṇava, and this [all] then stood empty. / That which is the form of the Lord, Śaṃkara, is himself Hari.

9.s:
śūnyām̐llokānimān dṛṣṭvā sisṛkṣurmūrttimuttamām .
kṣobhayitvā manodhāma tatrākāraḥ svamātrataḥ .. 9.8 ..
9.d:
शून्याम्̐ल्लोकानिमान् दृष्ट्वा सिसृक्षुर्मूर्त्तिमुत्तमाम् ।
क्षोभयित्वा मनोधाम तत्राकारः स्वमात्रतः ॥ 9.8 ॥
9.m: Seeing these worlds empty, wishing to create an excellent form, / having agitated the abode of mind, an appearance [arose] there from his own measure.

9.s:
sthitastasmin yadā kṣubdhe brahmāṇḍamabhavattadā .
tasmiṃstu śakalībhūte bhūrlokaṃ ca vyavasthitam .. 9.9 ..
9.d:
स्थितस्तस्मिन् यदा क्षुब्धे ब्रह्माण्डमभवत्तदा ।
तस्मिंस्तु शकलीभूते भूर्लोकं च व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 9.9 ॥
9.m: When it stood agitated in that, then the cosmic egg came into being; / and when that split into parts, the earth realm was established.

9.s:
aparaṃ bhuvanaṃ prāyānmadhye bhāskarasannibham .
purāṇapuruṣo vyāpya padmakośe vyavasthitaḥ .. 9.10 ..
9.d:
अपरं भुवनं प्रायान्मध्ये भास्करसन्निभम् ।
पुराणपुरुषो व्याप्य पद्मकोशे व्यवस्थितः ॥ 9.10 ॥
9.m:
Another realm became like the sun in the midst;
pervading it, the primal person took his stand in the lotus-calyx.

9.s:
sa hi nārāyaṇo devaḥ prājāpatyena tejasā .
akārādyaṃ svaraṃ nābhyāṃ halaṃ ca visasarja ha .. 9.11 ..
9.d:
स हि नारायणो देवः प्राजापत्येन तेजसा ।
अकाराद्यं स्वरं नाभ्यां हलं च विससर्ज ह ॥ 9.11 ॥
9.m:
Indeed, that divine Nārāyaṇa, with the radiance of Prajāpati,
emitted from his navel the vowels beginning with 'a' and the consonants.

9.s:
amūrttasṛṣṭau śāstrāṇi udagāyat tadā diśaḥ .
suṣṭvā punarameyātmā cintayāmāsa dhāraṇam .. 9.12 ..
9.d:
अमूर्त्तसृष्टौ शास्त्राणि उदगायत् तदा दिशः ।
सुष्ट्वा पुनरमेयात्मा चिन्तयामास धारणम् ॥ 9.12 ॥
9.m:
In the formless creation, he then chanted the scriptures to the directions;
having created [them], the immeasurable-souled one again thought upon sustaining [them].

9.s:
tasya cintayato netrāt tejaḥ samabhavanmahat .
dakṣiṇaṃ vahnisaṅkāśaṃ vāmaṃ tuhinasannibham .. 9.13 ..
9.d:
तस्य चिन्तयतो नेत्रात् तेजः समभवन्महत् ।
दक्षिणं वह्निसङ्काशं वामं तुहिनसन्निभम् ॥ 9.13 ॥
9.m:
As he was thinking, a great brilliance arose from his eye:
the right [resembling] fire, and the left resembling frost.

9.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā candrasūryau tu kalpitau parameṣṭhinā .
tataḥ prāṇaḥ samuttasthau vāyuśca parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 9.14 ..
9.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा चन्द्रसूर्यौ तु कल्पितौ परमेष्ठिना ।
ततः प्राणः समुत्तस्थौ वायुश्च परमेष्ठिनः ॥ 9.14 ॥
9.m:
Seeing that, the moon and the sun were fashioned by Parameṣṭhin;
then the breath of life and the wind arose from Parameṣṭhin.

9.s:
sa eva vāyurbhagavān yo'dyāpi hṛdigo vibhuḥ .
tasmād vahniḥ samuttasthau tasmādagnerjalaṃ mahat .. 9.15 ..
9.d:
स एव वायुर्भगवान् योऽद्यापि हृदिगो विभुः ।
तस्माद् वह्निः समुत्तस्थौ तस्मादग्नेर्जलं महत् ॥ 9.15 ॥
9.m:
That very wind is the Lord who even today is the all-pervading one in the heart;
from him arose fire, and from that fire great water.

9.s:
ya evāgniḥ sa vai tejo brāhmaṃ paramakāraṇam .
bāhubhyāmapyasau tejaḥ kṣātraṃ tejaḥ sasarja ha .. 9.16 ..
9.d:
य एवाग्निः स वै तेजो ब्राह्मं परमकारणम् ।
बाहुभ्यामप्यसौ तेजः क्षात्रं तेजः ससर्ज ह ॥ 9.16 ॥
9.m:
That very fire is indeed the brahminical energy, the ultimate cause;
from his two arms he also emitted the kṣatriya energy.

9.s:
ūrubhyāmapi vaiśyāṃśca padbhyāṃ śūdrāṃstathā vibhuḥ .
tatastu sasṛje yakṣān rākṣasāṃśca tathā vibhuḥ .. 9.17 ..
9.d:
ऊरुभ्यामपि वैश्यांश्च पद्भ्यां शूद्रांस्तथा विभुः ।
ततस्तु ससृजे यक्षान् राक्षसांश्च तथा विभुः ॥ 9.17 ॥
9.m:
From his two thighs the vaiśyas, and from his feet the śūdras likewise, the all-pervading one [created];
and then the all-pervading one created the yakṣas and rākṣasas.

9.s:
caturvidhaistu bhūrlokaṃ bhuvarlokaṃ viyaccaraiḥ .
bhūtaiḥ svarmārgagairanyaiḥ svarlokaṃ samapūrayat .. 9.18 ..
9.d:
चतुर्विधैस्तु भूर्लोकं भुवर्लोकं वियच्चरैः ।
भूतैः स्वर्मार्गगैरन्यैः स्वर्लोकं समपूरयत् ॥ 9.18 ॥
9.m:
He filled Bhūrloka with the four kinds [of beings], and Bhuvarloka with sky-farers;
with other beings going the heavenly path, he filled Svarloka.

9.s:
maharlokaṃ tathā taistairbhūtaiśca sanakādibhiḥ .
janolokaṃ tataścaiva vairājaiḥ samapūrayat .. 9.19 ..
9.d:
महर्लोकं तथा तैस्तैर्भूतैश्च सनकादिभिः ।
जनोलोकं ततश्चैव वैराजैः समपूरयत् ॥ 9.19 ॥
9.m:
Likewise Maharloka with those various beings, Sanaka and the rest;
and then he filled Janoloka with the Vairājas.

9.s:
tapolokaṃ tato devastaponiṣṭhairapūrayat .
apunarmārakairdevaiḥ satyalokamapūrayat .. 9.20 ..
9.d:
तपोलोकं ततो देवस्तपोनिष्ठैरपूरयत् ।
अपुनर्मारकैर्देवैः सत्यलोकमपूरयत् ॥ 9.20 ॥
9.m:
Then the god filled Tapoloka with those devoted to austerities;
and he filled Satyaloka with gods who never die again.

9.s:
sṛṣṭiṃ sṛṣṭvā tathā devo bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ .
kalpasaṃjñaṃ svakaṃ ghastraṃ jāgarti parameśvaraḥ .. 9.21 ..
9.d:
सृष्टिं सृष्ट्वा तथा देवो भगवान् भूतभावनः ।
कल्पसंज्ञं स्वकं घस्त्रं जागर्ति परमेश्वरः ॥ 9.21 ॥
9.m:
Thus having brought forth creation, the god, the Lord, creator of beings,
the supreme Lord remains awake during his own day known as a kalpa.

9.s:
tasmin jagati bhūrloko bhuvarlokaśca jāyate .
svarlokaśca trayo'pyete jāyante nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 9.22 ..
9.d:
तस्मिन् जगति भूर्लोको भुवर्लोकश्च जायते ।
स्वर्लोकश्च त्रयोऽप्येते जायन्ते नात्र संशयः ॥ 9.22 ॥
9.m:
In that world, Bhūrloka and Bhuvarloka are born,
and Svarloka—all three of these are born; there is no doubt here.

9.s:
supte tu deve kalpānte tāvatī rātririṣyate .
trai lokyametat suptaṃ syāt tathopaplavatāṃ gatam .. 9.23 ..
9.d:
सुप्ते तु देवे कल्पान्ते तावती रात्रिरिष्यते ।
त्रै लोक्यमेतत् सुप्तं स्यात् तथोपप्लवतां गतम् ॥ 9.23 ॥
9.m:
When the god sleeps at the end of the kalpa, a night of equal length is acknowledged;
this triple world must be asleep, and likewise submerged in deluge.

9.s:
tato rātryāṃ vyatītāyāmutthitaḥ kamalekṣaṇaḥ .
cintayāmāsa tān vedān mātaraṃ ca caturṣvapi .
cintayānaḥ sa deveśastān vedān nādhyagacchata .. 9.24 ..
9.d:
ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामुत्थितः कमलेक्षणः ।
चिन्तयामास तान् वेदान् मातरं च चतुर्ष्वपि ।
चिन्तयानः स देवेशस्तान् वेदान् नाध्यगच्छत ॥ 9.24 ॥

9.s:
lokamārgasthitiṃ karttuṃ nidrājñānena mohitaḥ .
cintayāmāsa deveśo nātra vedā vyavasthitāḥ .. 9.25 ..
9.d:
लोकमार्गस्थितिं कर्त्तुं निद्राज्ञानेन मोहितः ।
चिन्तयामास देवेशो नात्र वेदा व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 9.25 ॥
9.m:
In order to establish the way of the world, though bewildered by the ignorance of sleep,
the lord of the gods thought: 'The Vedas are not situated here.'

9.s:
tataḥ svamūrtau toyākhye līnān dṛṣṭvā sureśvaraḥ .
jighṛkṣuścintayāmāsa matsyo bhūtvāviśajjalam .. 9.26 ..
9.d:
ततः स्वमूर्तौ तोयाख्ये लीनान् दृष्ट्वा सुरेश्वरः ।
जिघृक्षुश्चिन्तयामास मत्स्यो भूत्वाविशज्जलम् ॥ 9.26 ॥
9.m:
Then, seeing them dissolved in his own water-form, the lord of gods,
wishing to seize them, reflected, and becoming a fish, entered the water.

9.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā mahāmatsyastatkṣaṇāt samajāyata .
viveśa ca jalaṃ devaḥ samantāt kṣobhayanniva .. 9.27 ..
9.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा महामत्स्यस्तत्क्षणात् समजायत ।
विवेश च जलं देवः समन्तात् क्षोभयन्निव ॥ 9.27 ॥
9.m:
Having meditated thus, he became a great fish in that very instant;
and the god entered the water, as if shaking it all around.

9.s:
tasmin praviṣṭe sahasā jalaṃ tu
mahāmahīdhṛgvapuṣi prakāśam .
mātsyaṃ gate devavare mahodadhiṃ
hariṃ stavaistuṣṭuvuruddhṛtakṣitim .. 9.28 ..
9.d:
तस्मिन् प्रविष्टे सहसा जलं तु
महामहीधृग्वपुषि प्रकाशम् ।
मात्स्यं गते देववरे महोदधिं
हरिं स्तवैस्तुष्टुवुरुद्धृतक्षितिम् ॥ 9.28 ॥
9.m:
When he had suddenly entered the water,
luminous in his form sustaining the great earth,
when the best of gods had assumed fish form in the great ocean,
they praised Hari, the upholder of the earth, with hymns:

9.s:
namo'stu vedāntaragāpratarkya
namo'stu nārāyaṇa matsyarūpa .
namo'stu te susvara viśvamūrtte
namo'stu vidyādvayarūpadhārin .. 9.29 ..
9.d:
नमोऽस्तु वेदान्तरगाप्रतर्क्य
नमोऽस्तु नारायण मत्स्यरूप ।
नमोऽस्तु ते सुस्वर विश्वमूर्त्ते
नमोऽस्तु विद्याद्वयरूपधारिन् ॥ 9.29 ॥
9.m:
"Obeisance to you who dwell in the Upanishads, beyond thought!
Obeisance to you, Nārāyaṇa in the form of a fish!
Obeisance to you of pleasant sound, whose form is the universe!
Obeisance to you who bear the form of the two kinds of knowledge!

9.s:
namo'stu candrārkamarutsvarūpa
jalāntaviśvasthita cārunetra .
namo'stu viṣṇoḥ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmaḥ
prapāhi no matsyatanuṃ vihāya .. 9.30 ..
9.d:
नमोऽस्तु चन्द्रार्कमरुत्स्वरूप
जलान्तविश्वस्थित चारुनेत्र ।
नमोऽस्तु विष्णोः शरणं व्रजामः
प्रपाहि नो मत्स्यतनुं विहाय ॥ 9.30 ॥
9.m:
Obeisance to you who are the forms of moon, sun, and wind,
dwelling in all that ends in water, lovely-eyed one!
